Countless souls scream in agonising harmony,
forever sinking under the weight of the newly dead.
description: (Custom Desecrated prefix) (Custom Desecrated prefix) (Custom Desecrated suffix) (Custom Desecrated suffix) (List of mods)

beginner.whatItIs: A diamond jewel carrying four custom desecrated modifiers drawn from a very large pool covering damage, recovery, minions, ailments and resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: With that many possible outcomes, no two of these are alike, so the jewel is judged entirely on the four lines it actually rolled.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When its four rolls happen to match what your build is short of. It is never a jewel you plan around before seeing it.

name: Heartbound Loop
explicitStats: 300 Physical Damage taken on Minion Death
flavourText:
When the axe finally fell, Seryl shared his pain,
and the last thought that flickered through his
fading mind was her broken, shattered scream.
description: Minions have (10-15)% increased maximum Life (10-15) Life Regeneration per second (20-40)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate 300 Physical Damage taken on Minion Death Minions Revive (10-15)% faster

beginner.whatItIs: A pearl ring with regeneration and cast speed that gives minions more life and a faster revive, and deals you three hundred physical damage every time a minion dies.
beginner.whyItMatters: The self-damage is fixed and unavoidable, so a build with fragile minions takes constant damage while a build with durable ones barely notices it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a summoner at level thirty-two with tough minions and a large life pool. It is lethal on a build whose minions die constantly.

name: Heatshiver
explicitStats: Gain 1% of Cold damage as Extra Fire damage per 1% Chill Magnitude on enemy
flavourText:
Give of your heated passions.
Give of your cold resolve.
You will be repaid.
description: (50-70)% increased Evasion Rating +(60-100) to maximum Mana +(20-30)% to Fire Resistance +(20-30)% to Cold Resistance Gain 1% of Cold damage as Extra Fire damage per 1% Chill Magnitude on enemy

beginner.whatItIs: A velvet cap with evasion, mana and both fire and cold resistance that adds fire damage on top of your cold damage, scaled to how heavily chilled the enemy is.
beginner.whyItMatters: The fire is added rather than taken out of the cold hit, so nothing is given up for it, and it rewards chilling an enemy hard before striking: applying a defensive ailment becomes the setup for your largest damage instead of a separate action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build at level fifty-two that chills deeply. Against enemies you cannot chill the helmet gives nothing extra.

name: Heroic Tragedy
explicitStats: Remembering (100-8000) songworthy deeds by the line of (Vorana-Medved-Olroth)
Passives in radius are Conquered by the Kalguur
flavourText:
They believed themselves courageous and selfless,
but that bravery became the doom at their door.
description: Remembering (100-8000) songworthy deeds by the line of (Vorana-Medved-Olroth) Passives in radius are Conquered by the Kalguur Historic

beginner.whatItIs: A timeless jewel that converts every passive in its radius into Kalguur passives, with the exact conversion decided by a number seeded into the jewel.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewrites a whole section of your tree rather than adding stats, so the same jewel socketed in two places produces two completely different results.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an established character willing to plan its tree around the conversion. Check what the radius actually becomes before spending points near it.

name: Hinekora's Sight
flavourText: Remember the past, anticipate the future.
description: +(300-600) to Accuracy Rating +(300-600) to Evasion Rating Cannot be Blinded

beginner.whatItIs: A stellar amulet giving several hundred accuracy rating and evasion rating, and making you impossible to blind.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blind slashes your chance to hit, so an attack build that has just spent its gear budget on accuracy can watch that investment vanish in the wrong fight. This closes that hole permanently.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear it on an accuracy-hungry attack build heading into content that blinds, and treat the evasion as a bonus rather than the reason to equip it.

name: Hoghunt
flavourText:
There was a very clear and delicious
reason why the Ezomytes chose to
stop their flight and settle in Phaaryl.
description: Adds (16-20) to (23-27) Physical Damage +15% to Critical Hit Chance 10% reduced Attack Speed +10 to Strength Maim on Critical Hit

beginner.whatItIs: A level one felled greatclub with high added physical damage and a very large critical hit chance bonus that maims enemies on a critical hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Maim slows the target, so critting on a slow two-handed weapon keeps enemies from closing or escaping between your swings.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one for levelling a critical melee build. Its slow attack speed makes it a weapon of few, heavy hits.

name: Horns of Bynden
explicitStats: Every Rage also grants 1% increased Armour
flavourText: The Younger Brother waded into Battle, shrugging off Blows.
description: +20 to Armour (5-15)% increased Rarity of Items found +(20-30) to Strength Gain 1 Rage on Melee Hit Every Rage also grants 1% increased Armour

beginner.whatItIs: A rusted greathelm at level one with strength, armour and item rarity that gains rage from melee hits and turns each point of rage into extra armour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a starting melee character a defence that grows as it fights, which is exactly the opposite of how the early game usually goes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on a melee build through the first acts, where a rising armour value covers your lack of gear.

name: Horror's Flight
explicitStats: Adds (19-23) to (31-37) Chaos Damage to Attacks
Gain 1 Fear Incarnate when you Cull a target
flavourText: If fear doesn't kill you, I will.
description: (200-300)% increased Evasion Rating (7-17)% increased Attack Speed +(13-23) to Dexterity Adds (19-23) to (31-37) Chaos Damage to Attacks Gain 1 Fear Incarnate when you Cull a target

beginner.whatItIs: Engraved bracers with heavy evasion, attack speed, dexterity and added chaos damage that grant a stack of Fear Incarnate whenever you cull a target.
beginner.whyItMatters: Culling happens at the end of a kill, so the gloves reward a build that finishes enemies quickly by feeding it a buff for doing so.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five attack build that already has a culling effect. Without one, the special line never triggers.

name: Hrimnor's Hymn
explicitStats: Slam Skills you use yourself cause an additional Aftershock
flavourText:
"The crack of bone, the spray of blood.
Is there sweeter music?"
- Hrimnor of the Ezomytes.
description: (80-120)% increased Physical Damage +(10-15) to Strength Gain (10-20) Life per enemy killed Slam Skills you use yourself cause an additional Aftershock

beginner.whatItIs: An oak greathammer with a large physical damage bonus, strength, life on kill and heavier stun buildup that makes your slam skills cause an extra aftershock.
beginner.whyItMatters: An additional aftershock is close to a free repeat of the slam, which is a very large early damage gain for a build built on slams.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level four on a slam build. It is one of the strongest levelling maces for a warrior, and does nothing for a strike build.

name: Hyrri's Ire
explicitStats: Gain (10-20)% of Damage as Extra Cold Damage
Evasion Rating is doubled if you have not been Hit Recently
flavourText:
Hyrri loosed a barrage of arrows,
tipped with a poisoned hatred
only oppression can ferment.
description: (100-150)% increased Evasion Rating Gain (10-20)% of Damage as Extra Cold Damage +(30-40) to Dexterity 25% increased Freeze Duration on Enemies Evasion Rating is doubled if you have not been Hit Recently

beginner.whatItIs: A high-level armoured vest that adds a slice of your damage as extra cold damage, extends freeze duration, and doubles your evasion rating whenever you have gone a moment without being hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties offence and defence to the same behaviour: freezing enemies stops them hitting you, and not being hit is exactly what keeps the doubled evasion active.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a ranged or high-mobility character at level seventy-three, especially one that already freezes. Its dexterity requirement is steep, so plan for it.

name: Hysseg's Claw
flavourText:
In a time of great need, surrounded by Abyssals,
the Wayward Druid came to the Sun Clan's aid.
It is a debt they have never forgotten.
description: (70-100)% increased Physical Damage 5% increased Movement Speed +(8-15) to Strength +(8-15) to Intelligence (5-8)% increased Damage per Minion

beginner.whatItIs: A familial talisman with physical damage, attributes and movement speed that increases minion damage and raises your own damage for each minion you have.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays you for your army rather than only paying the army, so a summoner that also fights gets stronger with every minion it adds.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a minion build whose character attacks too. With a small number of minions the personal bonus stays small.

name: Icefang Orbit
implicitStats: Adds 1 to 4 Physical Damage to Attacks
explicitStats: Adds (5-7) to (9-13) Physical Damage to Attacks
All Damage taken from Hits while Poisoned Contributes to Magnitude of Chill on you
All Damage from Hits against Poisoned targets Contributes to Chill Magnitude
(15-25)% increased Magnitude of Poison you inflict
flavourText:
Those members of the Brotherhood who employ the venom of
Trarthan ice snakes must take great care with the volatile substance.
description: Adds (5-7) to (9-13) Physical Damage to Attacks +(20-30) to Dexterity (10-20)% chance to Poison on Hit All Damage taken from Hits while Poisoned Contributes to Magnitude of Chill on you All Damage from Hits against Poisoned targets Contributes to Chill Magnitude (15-25)% increased Magnitude of Poison you inflict

beginner.whatItIs: An iron ring with added physical damage, dexterity and a poison chance that makes damage against poisoned enemies build chill, and damage you take while poisoned chill you.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links poison and chill in both directions, so poisoning enemies slows them down while being poisoned yourself becomes far more dangerous.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build at level thirty-six with chaos resistance capped. In poison-heavy content the second half of the ring works against you.

name: Icetomb
explicitStats: Gain Cold Thorns Damage equal to (10-18)% of your maximum Mana
flavourText:
When Solaris closes his burning eye
At the end of time,
the world will perish in ice.
description: +(20-30) to Strength +(20-30) to Intelligence +(30-40)% to Cold Resistance Gain Cold Thorns Damage equal to (10-18)% of your maximum Mana

beginner.whatItIs: Mail vestments with strength, intelligence and a large chunk of cold resistance that deal cold thorns damage scaled off your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: Thorns normally scale off nothing you were already building, so tying it to your mana pool lets a caster get real return damage from a stat it stacks anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-mana character being swarmed by melee monsters, from level sixteen. With a small mana pool the return damage is not worth the slot.

name: Idle Hands
explicitStats: 25% increased Attack Speed while on Full Mana
You count as on Full Mana while at 90% of maximum Mana or above
flavourText: The devil finds work for idle hands.
description: (40-60)% increased Evasion Rating +(60-100) to Accuracy Rating +(5-10) to Intelligence 25% increased Attack Speed while on Full Mana You count as on Full Mana while at 90% of maximum Mana or above

beginner.whatItIs: Sectioned bracers with evasion, accuracy and intelligence that give a large attack speed bonus while you are at full mana, and count you as full from ninety percent upwards.
beginner.whyItMatters: The ninety percent allowance is what makes the bonus usable, because a build that spends any mana at all would otherwise never qualify.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-eight on an attack build with cheap skills or strong regeneration. A mana-hungry build will sit below the threshold constantly.

name: Idol of Uldurn
flavourText:
Worship of house gods was tolerated
in Oriath, so long as it remained private.
description: +(60-80) to maximum Life +(10-20) to Dexterity Skills have +1 to Limit (40-20)% reduced Presence Area of Effect (10-15)% increased Spirit

beginner.whatItIs: A crimson amulet with life, dexterity, life regeneration and extra spirit, whose special line raises the limit on skills that can only have so many instances active at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: Skills capped by a limit, such as traps, totems or lingering effects, are held back by that number rather than by your damage, so one more instance is a direct output increase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build whose main skill has a hard limit printed on it. If nothing you use has a limit, the amulet is just life and spirit, and the reduced presence radius is a small penalty on top.

name: Igniferis
explicitStats: Life Recovery from Regeneration is not applied
Every 4 seconds, Recover 1 Life for every 0.2 Life Recovery per second from Regeneration
flavourText:
A hearth unyielding, ever warm,
A light unbroken, endlessly reborn.
description: +(10-20)% to Fire Resistance (20-30)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate 25% increased Light Radius Life Recovery from Regeneration is not applied Every 4 seconds, Recover 1 Life for every 0.2 Life Recovery per second from Regeneration

beginner.whatItIs: A crimson amulet with fire resistance and mana regeneration that turns off your regular life regeneration and instead pays it out as a lump of healing every four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Regeneration normally trickles in continuously, so bundling it into a periodic burst makes it much better against damage over time and much worse at topping you off between hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on a build with heavy regeneration that wants recovery in usable chunks. Avoid it if your regeneration is small, because a tiny trickle becomes a tiny burst that arrives too late.

name: Immaculate Adherence
explicitStats: 100% of Damage is taken from Mana before Life
Convert 100% of maximum Energy Shield to maximum Divinity
20% reduced maximum Divinity per Corrupted Item Equipped
Skills Cost Divinity instead of Mana or Life
flavourText: To stray is to condemn this world to sin.
description: 100% of Damage is taken from Mana before Life Cannot have Energy Shield Convert 100% of maximum Energy Shield to maximum Divinity (0-100)% increased maximum Divinity 20% reduced maximum Divinity per Corrupted Item Equipped Skills Cost Divinity instead of Mana or Life

beginner.whatItIs: A solar amulet that removes energy shield entirely, converts what you had into a resource called Divinity, and makes every skill spend Divinity while all damage hits your mana before your life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It replaces two of the game's core systems at once, so the character it makes is not a variation on a normal build but a separate one with its own rules for damage and casting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Build around it from the start, and keep corrupted items off your character, because each one shrinks your Divinity pool by a fifth.

name: Indigon
explicitStats: (10-15)% increased Spell damage for each 200 total Mana you have Spent Recently
(5-10)% increased Cost of Skills for each 200 total Mana Spent Recently
Mana Recovery other than Regeneration cannot Recover Mana
flavourText:
Where the body's limits begin,
the mind's limits end.
description: (100-140)% increased Energy Shield +(80-120) to maximum Mana (10-15)% increased Spell damage for each 200 total Mana you have Spent Recently (5-10)% increased Cost of Skills for each 200 total Mana Spent Recently Mana Recovery other than Regeneration cannot Recover Mana

beginner.whatItIs: A magus tiara with energy shield and mana that raises your spell damage and your skill costs together, based on how much mana you have spent recently, and blocks all mana recovery other than regeneration.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spending mana is both the damage engine and the danger, because costs climb as fast as damage does and you cannot use a flask to catch up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five caster built entirely around mana regeneration and spending. Without heavy regeneration the rising costs will lock you out of casting.

name: Ingenuity
explicitStats: (20-30)% increased bonuses gained from left Equipped Ring
(20-30)% increased bonuses gained from right Equipped Ring
flavourText:
Experiments with geomancy taught
the Maji more than they ever expected.
description: (-20-20)% increased Charm Charges gained (-10-10)% increased Charm Charges used (20-30)% increased bonuses gained from left Equipped Ring (20-30)% increased bonuses gained from right Equipped Ring

beginner.whatItIs: A utility belt that magnifies the bonuses coming from both of your equipped rings by a fifth to a third, on top of applying part of your flask recovery instantly.
beginner.whyItMatters: It multiplies gear you already own, so its worth is decided entirely by how strong your two rings are rather than by anything printed on the belt.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it once your rings carry big numbers worth amplifying. On a fresh character with cheap rings there is nothing for it to multiply.

name: Innsmouth
flavourText: Beyond madness lies inspiration.
description: +(20-30) to Evasion Rating 25% reduced maximum Mana +(10-20)% to Cold Resistance +(13-19)% to Chaos Resistance 100% increased Mana Regeneration Rate

beginner.whatItIs: A shabby hood at level one with evasion, cold resistance, chaos resistance and doubled mana regeneration, paid for with a quarter of your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: A smaller pool that refills much faster suits a caster spending mana constantly, and it hurts one that needs a large reserve for an expensive skill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on a caster with cheap, frequent spells. Skip it if any single skill costs a large share of your pool.

name: Ironbound
implicitStats: (25-35)% chance to Chain an additional time
explicitStats: (3-5)% increased Block chance per 100 total Item Armour on Equipped Armour Items
Hits with this weapon have (1-2) to (4-5) Added Physical Damage per 1% Block Chance
Arrows Return if they have Pierced a target which had Fully Broken Armour
flavourText:
Each crest was a Thane's word, bolted to Ivor's bow.
They would join the Count's side, or die by his hands.
description: +(100-150) to Armour (5-10)% increased Attack Speed +12% to Block chance (3-5)% increased Block chance per 100 total Item Armour on Equipped Armour Items Hits with this weapon have (1-2) to (4-5) Added Physical Damage per 1% Block Chance Arrows Return if they have Pierced a target which had Fully Broken Armour

beginner.whatItIs: A warden bow with armour and block chance that gains added physical damage for each point of block chance you have, and returns arrows that pierce a target with fully broken armour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It puts a bow in the hands of a blocking, armoured character and pays that character for the defensive stats it was already stacking.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a hybrid bow and shield build from level eleven that stacks armour on its gear. On a plain evasion archer the damage line barely triggers.

name: Irongrasp
flavourText: A power unknown aids your own.
description: (100-150)% increased Armour and Evasion +(20-30) to Strength +(100-150) to Stun Threshold Iron Grip Iron Will

beginner.whatItIs: A vagabond armour with strength, stun threshold and a large armour and evasion bonus that grants both Iron Grip and Iron Will.
beginner.whyItMatters: Those two keywords let strength add to projectile attack damage and to spell damage, so a single stat starts scaling parts of your build it normally has nothing to do with.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a strength-heavy character using projectiles or spells, from level sixteen. On a plain melee build both keywords do very little.

name: Ironride
explicitStats: You have no Accuracy Penalty at Distance
flavourText: Let the rider's aim be true.
description: (60-80)% increased Armour and Evasion +(30-50) to maximum Life +(30-50) to maximum Mana +(10-15)% to Lightning Resistance You have no Accuracy Penalty at Distance

beginner.whatItIs: A visored helm with armour, evasion, life, mana and lightning resistance that removes the accuracy penalty you normally take at long range.
beginner.whyItMatters: Attacks are less accurate the further away the target is, so a ranged attack build normally loses hits at exactly the distance it wants to fight from.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a bow or crossbow build that fights at maximum range. A melee character gains nothing from it.

name: Jarngreipr
explicitStats: Adds (2-3) to (5-6) Physical Damage to Attacks
Strength can satisfy other Attribute Requirements of Melee Weapons and Melee Skills
flavourText: The whispers of the old gods hum through the iron. They demand a hero.
description: 50% increased Armour and Evasion Adds (2-3) to (5-6) Physical Damage to Attacks +(30-50) to maximum Life (4-8)% increased Attack Speed Strength can satisfy other Attribute Requirements of Melee Weapons and Melee Skills

beginner.whatItIs: Ringmail gauntlets with life, attack speed and added physical damage that let strength satisfy the other attribute requirements of melee weapons and melee skills.
beginner.whyItMatters: It frees a pure strength character from chasing dexterity and intelligence just to equip things, which is often several passive points or a whole gear slot saved.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level six on a strength melee build. On a balanced attribute character there is nothing for the special line to solve.

name: Kalandra's Touch
flavourText: Power is a matter of perspective.
description: Reflects opposite Ring

beginner.whatItIs: A ring whose only line is that it copies whatever ring you are wearing in the opposite slot.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is worth exactly as much as your best ring, so upgrading one finger upgrades both at once and the ring itself is never the limiting factor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Once you own a single very strong ring worth having twice. Paired with an ordinary ring it is ordinary.

name: Kaltenhalt
explicitStats: Modifiers to Stun Buildup apply to Freeze Buildup instead for Parry
100% of Parry Physical Damage Converted to Cold Damage
flavourText: Cold, miserable and alone... but alive.
description: (80-120)% increased Evasion Rating +5% to Maximum Cold Resistance +(-40-40)% to Cold Resistance Modifiers to Stun Buildup apply to Freeze Buildup instead for Parry 100% of Parry Physical Damage Converted to Cold Damage 25 to 35 Cold Thorns damage

beginner.whatItIs: A ridged buckler that raises your maximum cold resistance, turns all parry physical damage into cold damage, applies your stun buildup as freeze buildup when parrying, and deals cold thorns damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts the whole parry mechanic into a freezing tool, so a defensive action becomes the way you lock enemies in place instead of just stopping a hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a parry build at level twenty-two leaning into cold. Check the cold resistance roll, because it can land at minus forty as easily as plus forty.

name: Kaom's Heart
flavourText: The warrior who fears will fall.
description: +1500 to maximum Life You have no Spirit

beginner.whatItIs: A conqueror plate with enormous armour that adds fifteen hundred maximum life and removes your spirit entirely.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spirit pays for reserved buffs, auras and minions, so the trade is not a stat swap but a decision to run none of them in exchange for a life pool nothing else can match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-eight melee character built purely on life and armour. If any part of your setup reserves spirit, this chest turns it off.

name: Keelhaul
explicitStats: Life Flasks gain 0.25 charges per Second
Mana Flasks gain 0.25 charges per Second
flavourText:
Below all living things,
there exists a flow...
description: (-25-25)% increased Flask Life Recovery rate (-25-25)% increased Flask Mana Recovery rate Life Flasks gain 0.25 charges per Second Mana Flasks gain 0.25 charges per Second

beginner.whatItIs: A starter linen belt whose life and mana flasks refill themselves steadily, with a recovery rate that can roll either up or down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Constantly regenerating charges mean you never arrive at a boss with empty flasks, which is the most common way an early character loses a fight it could have won.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear it from level one through the first acts. Check both recovery rolls, because a badly rolled pair makes each flask use noticeably weaker.

name: Keeper of the Arc
flavourText:
The priests of the Kalguur keep faith through numbers
and calculation, not unprovable promises.
description: (240-340)% increased Armour and Energy Shield (15-25) Life Regeneration per second (15-25)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Alternating every 5 seconds: Take 40% less Damage from Hits Take 40% less Damage over time

beginner.whatItIs: A spiritbone crown with very high defences and regeneration that alternates every five seconds between reducing hit damage and reducing damage over time by forty percent.
beginner.whyItMatters: You are always protected from one kind of damage and never from both, so the helmet is excellent against a fight that alternates and unreliable against one that does not.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-two character in mixed content. Against a boss whose damage is all hits or all degeneration, half the cycle is wasted.

name: Killjoy
explicitStats: Life Flasks do not recover Life
flavourText:
"Stitches? Wouldn't that defeat the purpose?"
- Jeffry, Torturer's Apprentice
description: (30-60)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield +(30-50) to maximum Life (20-30)% increased Critical Damage Bonus Life Flasks do not recover Life On-Kill Effects happen twice

beginner.whatItIs: Linen wraps with life, evasion, energy shield and critical damage that make every on-kill effect happen twice, at the price of life flasks healing nothing at all.
beginner.whyItMatters: Doubling on-kill effects is a large gain for a build stacked with them, and losing life flask healing removes the recovery most characters lean on hardest.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with several on-kill effects and a recovery plan that is not flasks, from level sixteen. It is dangerous on anything that flasks through damage.

name: Kingsguard
explicitStats: Recover 5% of maximum Life for each Endurance Charge consumed
flavourText: The toughest armour is the trust of your people.
description: +(60-80) to maximum Life +(40-60) to maximum Mana +(5-10)% to all Elemental Resistances 25% reduced Endurance Charge Duration Recover 5% of maximum Life for each Endurance Charge consumed

beginner.whatItIs: A full plate with life, mana and elemental resistance that heals five percent of your maximum life every time an endurance charge is consumed, while making those charges expire faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns endurance charges into a recovery mechanic on top of their usual damage reduction, so a build that spends them gets healed for doing what it already does.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character with a skill that consumes endurance charges, from level thirty-three. Without a consumer the healing line never fires.

name: Kitoko's Current
explicitStats: Lightning damage from Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup
flavourText: Reality is a puzzle. Ingenuity is power.
description: (30-50)% increased Energy Shield +(10-20) to Dexterity (15-10)% reduced Attack and Cast Speed Lightning damage from Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup

beginner.whatItIs: Jewelled gloves with energy shield and dexterity that make lightning damage from hits feed electrocution buildup, in exchange for slower attacks and casts.
beginner.whyItMatters: Electrocution is normally difficult to build up, and this gives a lightning character a direct route to it, though the speed penalty is felt on every action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build at level twenty-six aiming to electrocute enemies. On any other damage type the gloves are only a penalty.

name: Lavianga's Spirits
explicitStats: This Flask cannot be Used but applies its Effect constantly
flavourText:
"How do I cope with what I witnessed on Wraeclast?
Thank the Ancestors! My cup, it overflows."
- Lavianga, former advisor to Kaom
description: This Flask cannot be Used but applies its Effect constantly (80-70)% reduced Amount Recovered

beginner.whatItIs: A gargantuan mana flask that cannot be used at all and instead applies its effect constantly, at heavily reduced recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: Permanent uptime means any modifier on the flask is always active, which matters far more than the mana it restores.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty-nine when you want a flask modifier running all the time. As a source of mana recovery it is weak.

name: Leer Cast
explicitStats: Allies in your Presence deal 50% increased Damage
flavourText: For none of us are as cruel as all of us.
description: +(30-50) to maximum Life +(30-50) to maximum Mana Allies in your Presence deal 50% increased Damage +(10-20) to Dexterity 25% reduced Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A hooded mask with life, mana and dexterity that gives every ally in your presence a large damage bonus while cutting your own damage by a quarter.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a pure support piece: you give up a quarter of your own output to make everyone next to you noticeably stronger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For group play from level sixteen on a character that is not the party's damage dealer. Alone, it is a straight loss.

name: Legionstride
explicitStats: -10 Physical damage taken from Projectile Attacks
flavourText: A wall of steel and muscle.
description: +(50-70) to Armour +(50-70) to Stun Threshold -10 Physical damage taken from Projectile Attacks +10% to Block chance

beginner.whatItIs: Rough greaves available at level one with flat armour, stun threshold, block chance and a flat reduction to physical damage from projectile attacks.
beginner.whyItMatters: A flat reduction is huge against the small, fast projectiles that make up most early ranged damage, because it subtracts the same amount from every one of them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear them through the opening acts against archers and casters. They fall off once individual hits get large enough that a flat ten matters less.

name: Leopold's Applause
explicitStats: Your Hits can Penetrate Elemental Resistances down to a minimum of -50%
flavourText: "Keep smiling. The deepest cut comes not from insults, but from false praise."
description: (60-100)% increased Energy Shield +(60-100) to maximum Mana (10-15)% increased Rarity of Items found Damage Penetrates 10% Elemental Resistances Your Hits can Penetrate Elemental Resistances down to a minimum of -50%

beginner.whatItIs: Embroidered gloves with energy shield, mana and item rarity that penetrate a tenth of enemy elemental resistance and let your hits push that resistance as far as minus fifty percent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Raising the floor on penetration matters most against enemies you have already stripped, so the gloves scale with the rest of your resistance-reduction rather than working alone.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an elemental build at level fifty-two that already applies exposure or curses. On its own the ten percent is modest.

name: Levinstone
explicitStats: (10-20)% increased Magnitude of Shock you inflict
flavourText: Highgate held other secrets.
description: +(40-60) to maximum Mana (10-20)% increased chance to Shock Lightning Skills Chain +1 times (10-20)% increased Magnitude of Shock you inflict

beginner.whatItIs: A topaz ring with lightning resistance and mana that makes lightning skills chain an extra time and raises both your chance to shock and how deep those shocks go.
beginner.whyItMatters: An extra chain is a direct clear speed increase, and deeper shocks raise the damage everything takes from the same hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a lightning build clearing packs. Against a single target the chain line contributes nothing.

name: Lifesprig
explicitStats: +(1-3) to Level of all Spell Skills
Leeches 1% of maximum Life when you Cast a Spell
flavourText:
From the Smallest seeds
To the tallest redwoods
Life endures in Wraeclast.
description: +(10-20) to maximum Mana +(1-3) to Level of all Spell Skills (5-10)% increased Cast Speed Leeches 1% of maximum Life when you Cast a Spell

beginner.whatItIs: An attuned wand available at level two with mana, cast speed and several levels to all spell skills that leeches a small share of your life every time you cast.
beginner.whyItMatters: Skill levels raise base damage rather than adding a percentage, so a few of them this early is a much larger gain than the small numbers suggest.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level two for levelling any caster, and the leech on cast quietly keeps you topped up while you clear.

name: Lightning Coil
explicitStats: (30-50)% of Physical damage from Hits taken as Lightning damage
flavourText:
The world churned during the Great Wasting.
Tawhoa may have stilled the rioting earth,
but it was Valako that tamed the broken sky.
description: (80-120)% increased Armour +(80-100) to maximum Life +(20-30) to Dexterity -(40-30)% to Lightning Resistance (30-50)% of Physical damage from Hits taken as Lightning damage

beginner.whatItIs: An ancestral mail with armour and life that reroutes a third to a half of the physical damage you take into lightning damage, and drops your lightning resistance sharply.
beginner.whyItMatters: Physical damage is the hardest kind to reduce, so converting it into an element you can resist is a real defensive gain, provided you have the resistance to absorb it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it at level sixty-five only once your lightning resistance is comfortably at the cap after the penalty. Below the cap it converts damage into a form that hurts you more.

name: Ligurium Talisman
explicitStats: Life Regeneration is applied to Energy Shield instead
flavourText: Healing the soul requires sacrifice.
description: +(30-40) to maximum Energy Shield +(25-35) to Spirit +(20-30) to Intelligence Life Regeneration is applied to Energy Shield instead

beginner.whatItIs: A lapis amulet with energy shield, spirit and intelligence that redirects your life regeneration into your energy shield instead.
beginner.whyItMatters: Energy shield normally refuses to recharge for several seconds after you take a hit, so a source that refills it continuously fixes the single biggest weakness of shield-based defence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it on an energy shield character that has picked up regeneration from the passive tree or elsewhere. With no regeneration to redirect the line does nothing at all.

name: Liminal Coil
explicitStats: Magnitudes of Curses you inflict are zero
Curses you inflict ignore Curse limit
Spell Hits Gain (23-31)% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage per Curse on target
Spell Hits Gain (23-31)% of Damage as Extra Physical Damage per Curse on target
flavourText:
In that moment, Viridi's bones became
branches, weaving over the Darkness.
She coiled around the nothing,
trapping it within her everything.
description: (71-113)% increased Spell Damage (7-13)% increased Cast Speed Magnitudes of Curses you inflict are zero Curses you inflict ignore Curse limit Spell Hits Gain (23-31)% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage per Curse on target Spell Hits Gain (23-31)% of Damage as Extra Physical Damage per Curse on target

beginner.whatItIs: A twisted wand with spell damage and cast speed that reduces the magnitude of your curses to nothing, lets them ignore the curse limit, and adds chaos and physical damage to your spell hits for each curse on the target.
beginner.whyItMatters: Your curses stop doing anything on their own and become counters that raise your spell damage, so stacking many weak curses is the entire point.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five caster that can apply several curses quickly. A build relying on curse effects loses them completely.

name: Lioneye's Glare
explicitStats: +2 metres to Dodge Roll distance if you haven't Dodge Rolled Recently
-1 metre to Dodge Roll distance if you've Dodge Rolled Recently
Repeatable Attacks with this Bow Repeat +2 times if no enemies are in your Presence
flavourText:
"Kinslayer, you dishonour your own traditions to turn the tide of battle!
Let us see which is stronger... Karui savagery or the might of the Empire!"
- General Marceus Lioneye
description: (150-240)% increased Physical Damage +(300-500) to Accuracy Rating 10% increased Attack Speed +(20-30) to Dexterity +2 metres to Dodge Roll distance if you haven't Dodge Rolled Recently -1 metre to Dodge Roll distance if you've Dodge Rolled Recently Repeatable Attacks with this Bow Repeat +2 times if no enemies are in your Presence

beginner.whatItIs: A heavy bow with very high physical damage and accuracy that lengthens your first dodge roll, shortens the next one, and repeats attacks two extra times when no enemies are near you.
beginner.whyItMatters: The repeat line pays out at range, so the bow is at its best when you are shooting into a fight you are not standing in, which is exactly how a bow wants to be played.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five bow build using a repeatable attack, played at distance. Fighting in melee turns off the repeats entirely.

name: Lochtonial Caress
explicitStats: Share Charges with Allies in your Presence
flavourText:
Why cling to your sanity? It offers you nothing.
Surrender to me, and I will grant you everything.
description: (10-15)% increased Skill Speed +(15-25) to Armour +(40-60) to maximum Life (15-10)% reduced maximum Mana Share Charges with Allies in your Presence

beginner.whatItIs: Tempered mitts with armour, life and skill speed that share your charges with allies standing in your presence, at the cost of some maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: Charges are normally personal, so handing them to your party turns your generation into a group buff without you giving anything up except mana.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For group play from level sixteen on a character that generates charges quickly. Alone, the sharing line does nothing.

beginner.whatItIs: An ornate ringmail that rolls three random unique ring modifiers and sets all four of your maximum resistances to a single rolled value between seventy-five and eighty percent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Maximum resistance is a ceiling on every point of resistance you own, so five percentage points between the worst and the best roll is a far larger defensive swing than the size of the number suggests.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only worth the slot with a maximum resistance roll near the top of its range and ring modifiers your build wants. Read all four lines before equipping, since two of these are never the same.

name: Luminous Pace
explicitStats: 100% faster start of Energy Shield Recharge
flavourText: Blessed are those who tend the Grove.
description: 10% increased Movement Speed +(20-30) to maximum Energy Shield +(5-10) to Intelligence (30-20)% reduced Energy Shield Recharge Rate 100% faster start of Energy Shield Recharge

beginner.whatItIs: Straw sandals at level one with movement speed, energy shield and intelligence that start your shield recharge much sooner but recharge it more slowly once it begins.
beginner.whyItMatters: Getting the recharge started is the hard part in a fight, so beginning it sooner usually means more shield restored overall even at the lower rate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a starting energy shield character that takes frequent small hits. A build facing rare, huge hits would rather have the faster rate.

name: Lycosidae
explicitStats: Blocking Damage Poisons the Enemy as though dealing 200 Base Chaos Damage
flavourText: A true predator does not chase; It waits.
description: (10-15)% increased Block chance (60-100)% increased Armour Accuracy Rating is Doubled Blocking Damage Poisons the Enemy as though dealing 200 Base Chaos Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A rampart tower shield with block chance and armour that doubles your accuracy rating and poisons enemies whose damage you block.
beginner.whyItMatters: Doubling accuracy is a large offensive gain from a defensive slot, which is what lets an armoured attacker skip accuracy elsewhere on its gear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-eight on an attack build struggling to hit. It gives a caster nothing but the block and armour.

name: Mageblood
explicitStats: All Mage's Legacies have (25-50)% increased effect per duplicate Mage's Legacy you have
flavourText:
Rivers of power coursed through their veins.
Now, that power is yours, for good or ill.
description: (Random Mage's Legacy modifier) (Random Mage's Legacy modifier) (Random Mage's Legacy modifier) (Random Mage's Legacy modifier) All Mage's Legacies have (25-50)% increased effect per duplicate Mage's Legacy you have

beginner.whatItIs: A utility belt that rolls four random Mage's Legacy modifiers and makes each of them stronger for every duplicate you are carrying.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two copies of the same legacy are worth much more than two different ones, so the belt rewards a lucky roll rather than a good one, and no two of these are alike.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Read the four rolls before you commit the slot. It is a strong belt when the duplicates line up with your build and an ordinary one when they do not.

name: Mahuxotl's Machination
explicitStats: (66-333)% increased effect of Socketed Soul Cores
flavourText: The Banished Architect sought to employ the darkest secrets of the Vaal.
description: (333-666)% increased Armour and Energy Shield (66-333)% increased effect of Socketed Soul Cores Everlasting Sacrifice Has 2 Augment Sockets (Hidden)

beginner.whatItIs: An omen crest shield with an enormous defence range, two hidden augment sockets, greatly increased soul core effect, and the Everlasting Sacrifice keyword.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its rolls span a huge range and the soul cores you socket decide most of its power, so two of these can differ by several times over.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty-eight when you own soul cores worth amplifying and the roll is high. At the low end it is an ordinary shield.

name: Maligaro's Virtuosity
explicitStats: Your Critical Hit Chance cannot be Rerolled
flavourText:
Maligaro operated effortlessly,
with great speed and terrible consequences.
description: (60-80)% increased Evasion Rating (20-30)% increased Critical Hit Chance 5% increased Attack Speed +(10-20) to Dexterity Your Critical Damage Bonus is 250% Your Critical Hit Chance cannot be Rerolled

beginner.whatItIs: Fine bracers with evasion, critical hit chance, attack speed and dexterity that fix your critical damage bonus at two hundred and fifty percent and stop your critical chance being rerolled.
beginner.whyItMatters: A fixed critical damage bonus is a floor and a ceiling at once: it is very strong early and becomes a cap once your own critical damage would have grown past it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty-five on a critical build that has not yet invested in critical damage. Retire them once your own bonus would exceed the fixed value.

name: Marohi Erqi
explicitStats: Heavy Stuns Enemies that are on Full Life
flavourText: "Drunken Erqi boasted to Tukohama; the God of War challenged him to a clash of strength. Woe to the Divine - he should have made it a test of skill!"
description: +150 Strength Requirement (600-700)% increased Physical Damage -(300-200) to Accuracy Rating 35% reduced Attack Speed Causes (40-60)% increased Stun Buildup Heavy Stuns Enemies that are on Full Life

beginner.whatItIs: A totemic greatclub with an enormous physical damage bonus that heavily stuns enemies at full life, at the cost of accuracy, attack speed and a steep strength requirement.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is built around one huge, slow, inaccurate hit, so it wants a build that lands rarely and heavily rather than one that swings often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty slam or stun build with accuracy from elsewhere. Its accuracy penalty is severe enough to need answering.

name: Mask of the Sanguimancer
explicitStats: (20-40)% increased Critical Hit Chance for Spells
flavourText:
A terror of ancient times, his identity
remains lost... but his power does not.
description: +(20-25) to Evasion Rating +(10-15) to maximum Energy Shield (20-40)% increased Critical Hit Chance for Spells +(10-20) to Strength +(10-20) to Intelligence Blood Magic

beginner.whatItIs: A face mask with evasion, energy shield, attributes and spell critical chance that grants Blood Magic.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blood Magic makes your skills cost life instead of mana, which removes the mana problem entirely and puts every cast on the same bar that keeps you alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level ten on a build with a large life pool and strong recovery. On a fragile character the cost of every cast becomes the reason you die.

name: Mask of the Stitched Demon
explicitStats: Regenerate 0.05 Life per second per Maximum Energy Shield
flavourText:
From the flesh of the gods, Xibaqua was born.
From the carnage of Xibaqua, we were born.
It is our duty to return to the gods what was once theirs.
description: (120-160)% increased Energy Shield +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance Cannot have Energy Shield Regenerate 0.05 Life per second per Maximum Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: A feathered tiara with a large energy shield bonus and chaos resistance that then stops you having any energy shield at all, and instead regenerates life in proportion to what your maximum shield would have been.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts an entire shield pool into constant life regeneration, so every energy shield roll on your gear becomes healing rather than a buffer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level thirty-three life build stacking energy shield rolls purely for the regeneration. It is a trap on a character that actually wants a shield.

explicitStats: Area counts as (Random map biome) Biome

flavourText:
"For a brief shining time, the Precursors
could resculpt the world as they saw fit."
description: Area counts as (Random map biome) Biome

beginner.whatItIs: An irradiated tablet with a single use that makes the area also count as a randomly chosen biome.
beginner.whyItMatters: Biome-specific content only appears in the right kind of area, so this lets a map you already have qualify for something it otherwise could not.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the rolled biome matches the content you are chasing. Check the roll before spending the single use.

name: Matsya
flavourText: In our tales, and in our hearts, the rivers still flow.
description: Adds (6-9) to (10-15) Cold Damage Adds 1 to (19-29) Lightning Damage +(3-5)% to Critical Hit Chance (15-20)% increased Attack Speed (25-40)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Skills reserve 50% less Spirit

beginner.whatItIs: A crescent quarterstaff with added cold and lightning damage, critical hit chance and mana regeneration that halves the spirit your skills reserve.
beginner.whyItMatters: Halved reservation is effectively double the spirit, so a build can run buffs or minions it could not otherwise afford while still holding a real weapon.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty on any build reserving spirit heavily. If you reserve nothing, the weapon is only its damage rolls.

name: Megalomaniac
flavourText:
If you're going to act like you're better
than everyone else, make sure you are.
description: Allocates (2-3 random notable passive skills)

beginner.whatItIs: A diamond jewel that allocates two or three random notable passive skills for you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Notables are normally the expensive end of a passive path, so getting two or three for one socket can save a very large number of points, if they are ones you wanted.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when the rolled notables suit your build. Two irrelevant notables make it a blank jewel.

name: Meginord's Girdle
flavourText:
Kaom's strength was rivaled only by
the great Meginord of the north.
description: +(40-50) to Strength +(10-15)% to Cold Resistance 50% increased Flask Charges used 100% increased Flask Charges gained

beginner.whatItIs: A rawhide belt available from level one that gives a very large amount of strength and some cold resistance, and makes flasks both gain and spend charges much faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forty to fifty strength that early is worth a whole cluster of passive points, and for most characters it is the fastest route to the strength requirements on heavy armour.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear it through the campaign on any strength-based character. The faster charge use is a fair trade because charges also come in twice as quickly.

name: Melting Maelstrom
explicitStats: Effect is not removed when Unreserved Mana is Filled
Every 3 seconds during Effect, deal 100% of Mana spent in those seconds as Chaos Damage to Enemies within 3 metres
Deals 25% of current Mana as Chaos Damage to you when Effect ends
flavourText: What is life, but a dreamlike spiral of panic?
description: Effect is not removed when Unreserved Mana is Filled (200-250)% increased Duration Every 3 seconds during Effect, deal 100% of Mana spent in those seconds as Chaos Damage to Enemies within 3 metres Deals 25% of current Mana as Chaos Damage to you when Effect ends

beginner.whatItIs: An ultimate mana flask that lasts much longer, converts the mana you spend into chaos damage around you every three seconds, and hits you for a quarter of your current mana when it ends.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns your casting costs into area damage, so a mana-hungry caster gets a second damage source out of the spending it was already doing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty caster with high mana spending and enough chaos resistance to survive the ending hit.

name: Midnight Braid
explicitStats: 50% of Damage taken Recouped as Mana
flavourText:
Adversity is the soil in
which persistence grows.
description: +(30-50) to maximum Mana +(5-10)% to all Elemental Resistances 50% of Damage taken Recouped as Mana

beginner.whatItIs: A starter rawhide belt with maximum mana and a little elemental resistance that pays half the damage you take back into your mana pool.
beginner.whyItMatters: Recouping damage as mana turns every hit you survive into fuel for the next spell, which quietly removes the mana problem an early caster otherwise fights all campaign.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spellcaster from level one, and it stays useful for any build that spends mana faster than it regenerates it.

name: Mind of the Council
explicitStats: Attacks cost an additional 6% of your maximum Mana
Attacks have Added maximum Lightning Damage equal to (6-9)% of maximum Mana
flavourText:
The sky tore asunder, black cleaving upon blue
The end of life, of Time, with no escape
But they found a fragment, a void, a haven
And there they waited, as it all began again
Dark will, dark knowledge, enemies of Fate
They know your mind, because they remember
description: (150-200)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield +(60-90) to maximum Mana +(20-30)% to Lightning Resistance Attacks cost an additional 6% of your maximum Mana Attacks have Added maximum Lightning Damage equal to (6-9)% of maximum Mana

beginner.whatItIs: A death mask with evasion, energy shield, mana and lightning resistance that makes attacks cost extra mana and adds lightning damage to them based on your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns mana into an attack damage stat, so an attack build starts caring about a resource it normally spends almost nothing on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-mana attack build at level sixty-five. With a small pool you pay the extra cost and receive very little damage for it.

name: Ming's Heart
explicitStats: Gain (30-40)% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage
flavourText:
Ming slew Tranquillity
Took Chaos for his wife
And on Her immortal finger
He placed his Heart
description: 20% reduced maximum Life Gain (30-40)% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage 30% reduced Global Defences

beginner.whatItIs: An amethyst ring with chaos resistance that adds a large slice of your damage as extra chaos damage, in exchange for a fifth of your maximum life and a third of your defences.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a straightforward trade of survivability for damage, and the defensive cost applies to armour, evasion and energy shield alike rather than to one of them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty on a build that kills quickly and does not intend to be hit. It is a poor choice for anything learning a fight.

name: Mist Whisper
flavourText:
Sibilant promises surrounded them in the night.
All the travelers had to give him was their devotion...
description: Adds (8-10) to (13-15) Cold Damage Gain 5 Mana per enemy killed (30-50)% increased Freeze Buildup 30% increased Chill Duration on Enemies Attacks Chain 2 additional times

beginner.whatItIs: A level one makeshift crossbow with added cold damage that chains its attacks two extra times, builds freeze faster and returns mana on kill.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaining lets a single shot hit several enemies, which is a level of clear speed a starting character has almost no other way to reach.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one through the opening acts, especially on a cold build that wants the freeze buildup as a defensive tool.

name: Mjölner
explicitStats: +(2-4) to Level of all Lightning Skills
flavourText: Look the storm in the eye and you will have its respect.
description: +200 Intelligence Requirement +100 Strength Requirement (250-350)% increased Physical Damage (10-20)% increased Attack Speed +(2-4) to Level of all Lightning Skills

beginner.whatItIs: A torment club with very high physical damage, attack speed and several levels to all lightning skills, gated behind steep strength and intelligence requirements.
beginner.whyItMatters: Levels on lightning skills raise their base damage, so this is a rare weapon that scales a caster's spells while still hitting hard as a mace.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five hybrid attack and lightning build. Its combined attribute requirements are among the hardest to meet on any weapon.

name: Morior Invictus
explicitStats: (300-400)% increased Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield

beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five character that owns the augments to fill it. Unfilled, it is defences and nothing else, so budget for the sockets before the chest.

They're actually for brewing poisons."

beginner.whatItIs: A toxic quiver with added physical damage, mana on kill and a high chance to poison that blinds any target you poison.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blinding through poison means your damage over time also lowers the enemy's chance to hit you, so one effect covers offence and defence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison bow build from level thirty-nine, especially against packs of melee enemies that have to reach you.

beginner.whatItIs: A covert hood with evasion, accuracy and mana that doubles the life threshold at which culling strike kills an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Culling normally finishes enemies below a tenth of their life, and doubling that means bosses die from a much larger remaining health bar.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty-six build that already has culling strike. Without a culling source the helmet's main line does nothing.

name: Nascent Hope

Energy Shield Recharge starts on use

beginner.whyItMatters: It answers a freeze and refills your shield with the same button, so the moment you break out of the freeze you are also back at full defences.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an energy shield character from level twelve in cold content. It is close to useless on a build with no energy shield to recharge.

name: Nazir's Judgement
explicitStats: (35-50)% increased Melee Damage against Heavy Stunned enemies
flavourText: The first witch hunter knew one critical tactic: never let your enemy have a clear moment.

beginner.whatItIs: A steelpoint quarterstaff with very high added physical damage and accuracy that dazes on hit, lengthens stuns, and deals much more melee damage to heavily stunned enemies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It builds its own setup: daze and stun come from the same hits that then benefit from the target being stunned.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-eight on a melee build against enemies that can be stunned. Bosses with high stun thresholds get much less out of it.

name: Nebuloch
explicitStats: Attacks consume an Endurance Charge to Critically Hit
Take 100 Chaos damage per second per Endurance Charge
flavourText:
They hoped that, trapped in its prison,
the creature would age and perish.
But time would not touch the fiend.

beginner.whatItIs: An execratus hammer with large added physical and chaos damage that spends an endurance charge to land a critical hit and burns you for chaos damage every second for each charge you hold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endurance charges become ammunition for your crits and a running cost to your life at the same time, so holding them is both your damage and your danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty-five build that generates endurance charges quickly and has chaos resistance capped. Without generation your crits stop entirely.

name: Necromantle
explicitStats: Minions gain (20-30)% of their maximum Life as Extra maximum Energy Shield
flavourText:
Fueled by the blackness in the hearts of men,
the armies of Saresh were just as relentless.

beginner.whatItIs: A bone raiment with life and mana that gives your minions chaos resistance, extra energy shield on top of their life, and a much faster revive.
beginner.whyItMatters: Minion deaths cost a summoner damage while they are down, so a revive rate half again as fast, plus chaos resistance on the minions themselves, keeps your army on the field during the fights that kill it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build from level sixteen, and it stays useful long past that level because nothing on it is a raw number that gets outscaled.

name: Ngamahu's Chosen

beginner.whatItIs: A ruby charm that triggers when fire damage hits you, fills you to maximum rage on use, and gains charges faster than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rage is normally built slowly by attacking, and this hands you a full bar the moment you are hurt, so being hit becomes the fastest way to get to full power.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage build from level five fighting fire enemies. Without a rage payoff the charm is just a fire trigger with nothing behind it.

name: Nightfall
explicitStats: (10-20)% of Fire damage taken as Cold damage
(10-20)% of Lightning damage taken as Cold damage
flavourText:
"Upon plains of endless chill,
They Who Never Tire... dominate.
They Who Never Surrender... terrify.
And They Who Lay Beneath... wait for Nightfall."
- Tul, She That Silences

beginner.whatItIs: A glacial fortress with a very high armour bonus, block chance and cold resistance that converts part of the fire and lightning damage you take into cold damage, behind a steep strength requirement.
beginner.whyItMatters: Funnelling two elements into a third means one high resistance covers three, so stacking cold resistance protects you from far more than cold.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level seventy strength build with cold resistance well above the cap. Without that overcap the conversion just moves damage sideways.

flavourText: Diamora sings not for hunger, but for longing.

beginner.whatItIs: Pauascale gloves with energy shield, critical hit chance, intelligence and cold resistance that give a huge mana regeneration bonus after a critical hit and stop mana regeneration entirely without one.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes critical hits your mana supply, so a fight where you fail to crit quickly becomes a fight where you cannot cast at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a reliable critical caster at level forty-five with high critical chance. On a build that crits occasionally the penalty is far worse than the bonus.

name: Nocturne
explicitStats: Parried enemies take more Spell Damage instead of more Attack Damage
flavourText:
Light and shadow chase eternal,
but neither knows the other exists...

beginner.whatItIs: A wooden buckler with mana, elemental resistance and accuracy that makes parried enemies take more spell damage rather than more attack damage, and doubles how long that debuff lasts.
beginner.whyItMatters: Parry is normally a melee attacker's setup tool, and this hands the payoff to a spellcaster, which is the only way a caster gets anything out of parrying.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spellcaster willing to parry from level five. On an attack build the swap takes away the bonus you actually wanted.

name: Northpaw

description: +(15-25) to Evasion Rating Adds (3-5) to (8-10) Physical Damage to Attacks (10-15)% increased Critical Damage Bonus Base Critical Hit Chance for Attacks with Weapons is 7%

beginner.whatItIs: Suede bracers available at level one that add physical damage and critical damage, and set your base critical hit chance with weapons to seven percent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Setting the base chance applies before every percentage bonus you own, so it lifts the whole critical calculation rather than adding to the end of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on a weapon build that wants to crit, and especially on weapons whose own base critical chance is low.

name: Oaksworn
flavourText: The druids swore to protect the Grelwood with their very lives.
description: (20-30)% increased Block chance (80-120)% increased Armour and Energy Shield 50% increased Life Regeneration rate +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance

beginner.whatItIs: A sigil crest shield with block chance, armour, energy shield and chaos resistance that increases your life regeneration rate by half.
beginner.whyItMatters: Multiplying regeneration is worth more the more of it you have, so it turns a modest regeneration build into a genuinely self-sustaining one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level seven on a build with real life regeneration. With very little regeneration there is nothing to multiply.

name: Obern's Bastion
flavourText: The storm cannot sway those of sure footing.
description: (150-200)% increased Armour and Evasion (20-25) Life Regeneration per second 200% increased Stun Recovery (30-50)% reduced Chill Duration on you (30-50)% reduced Freeze Duration on you (30-50)% reduced Shock duration on you

beginner.whatItIs: Stacked sabatons with armour, evasion and life regeneration that recover from stuns much faster and cut the duration of chill, freeze and shock on you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being locked in place is what kills slow characters, and this shortens every source of that at once rather than answering one element at a time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level thirty-three on a slow melee character, especially in content that layers several ailments on you at once.

beginner.whatItIs: An ultimate life flask that gains charges much faster, regenerates runic ward while it is active, and converts your current runic ward into a guard buff when it ends.
beginner.whyItMatters: It builds a defensive buffer over the whole flask duration and then hands it to you as guard, so the payoff arrives after the flask is finished rather than during it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty build with runic ward, drunk before a dangerous phase rather than in the middle of one.

name: Olrovasara

beginner.whyItMatters: The weapon gets stronger during a fight rather than arriving strong, so it favours long encounters against powerful targets over quick clears.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five build fighting rare and unique enemies. Against trash the buildup ends before it matters.

beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty build using skills with a timing window. On a build with no such skills the flask never triggers at all.

beginner.whatItIs: An amethyst ring with heavy chaos resistance that converts all of your elemental damage into chaos damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage is resisted by far fewer enemies than the elements, so full conversion can be a large practical damage increase even with no extra numbers attached.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty on an elemental build with no scaling tied to a specific element. Any penetration or ailment built around fire, cold or lightning stops working.

beginner.whatItIs: Torn gloves at level one that split your elemental damage evenly into fire, cold and lightning, and add a slice of each element back on top.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spreading damage across all three elements means no single enemy resistance blunts your whole output, and it lets one build apply all three elemental ailments.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on an elemental build that wants coverage rather than a single element. A build stacking one element's penetration loses more than it gains.

"We sometimes fail. We sometimes succeed. Who determines one from the other?

beginner.whatItIs: A shrine sceptre that adds chaos damage to your hits and to your allies' attacks, grants the effect of a Dreaming Gloom Shrine, and can roll skill effect duration either up or down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage is resisted by far fewer enemies than the elements, so the damage it hands out is less likely to be blunted by whatever you are fighting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level sixty-five in a party, and check the duration roll, which can land negative.

name: Pariah's Embrace

His isolation caused him to treasure
their companionship all the more.

beginner.whatItIs: A cloaked mail with armour, attributes and life regeneration that grants fifty spirit and makes your skills spend mana more efficiently.
beginner.whyItMatters: It solves two resource problems at once, so a build that was choosing between an aura and its mana costs can afford both without changing anything else.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-six on any character short on spirit or struggling to sustain mana. It is a solid all-round chest rather than a build-defining one.

name: Perandus Seal

beginner.whatItIs: A gold ring with mana, all three attributes, item rarity and increased gold dropped by enemies you kill.
beginner.whyItMatters: Gold pays for the things currency does not, so a ring that raises both rarity and gold is a farming tool rather than a combat one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty while farming content you already clear. Swap it out for a defensive ring in anything dangerous.

beginner.whatItIs: A knight armour with a very large armour and evasion bonus that gives a chance to avoid hits of every damage type outright, and intimidates enemies standing near you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Avoidance applies before anything else, so it works equally against a small hit and a lethal one, which is the kind of defence armour alone cannot provide.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty-five character taking damage from mixed sources. Check the five rolls, because the range between a low and a high roll is very wide.

beginner.whatItIs: A heartwood shortbow with large added fire, cold and lightning damage that makes all elemental hit damage feed flammability, ignite, chill, freeze and shock at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: Normally each ailment is built by its own element, and this lets one attack push every ailment forward together, so a mixed elemental bow applies all of them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an elemental bow build at level sixty-seven aiming to lock enemies down with ailments rather than to kill them with a single element.

name: Pillar of the Caged God

flavourText:
Forged to rule the waves and tide
Destined to serve the monkey's paw
Strong as a tower of iron
Deft as the needle doubt

beginner.whatItIs: A long quarterstaff with almost no damage of its own that scales weapon damage with strength, attack speed with dexterity and area of effect with intelligence.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns raw attributes into every part of your attack, so a character that stacks all three stats ends up with numbers no ordinary weapon reaches.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an attribute-stacking build from level four. On a character with normal attribute totals it stays a weak level four staff.

name: Plaguefinger
explicitStats: All Damage from Hits Contributes to Poison Magnitude
flavourText: Ulcers, scabs, and pocks, the third army makes its claim.

beginner.whatItIs: Gauze wraps with evasion, energy shield and attack speed that stop you inflicting elemental ailments entirely and instead make all of your hit damage feed poison.
beginner.whyItMatters: Normally only physical and chaos damage builds poison, so this lets an elemental or mixed build poison at full strength, at the price of every ailment it used to apply.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build from level four. Any build that relies on freezing, shocking or igniting loses that entirely.

name: Polcirkeln

flavourText:
I rule the north
A legacy earned
Time and time again
Sing Meginord's song!

beginner.whatItIs: A sapphire ring with cold resistance, cold damage, mana and strength that lets enemies chilled by your hits shatter as though they had been frozen.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shattering removes the corpse entirely, which stops anything that revives, explodes or feeds on bodies, and it happens from a chill rather than a full freeze.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twelve on a cold build fighting enemies that use corpses. It also keeps the screen clear while mapping.

name: Powertread
explicitStats: 12% increased Critical Damage Bonus per Power Charge
flavourText:
The combat stance used by Vaal nobles
was as elegant as it was deadly.
description: (15-20)% increased Movement Speed (60-80)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield +(10-20) to Intelligence +1 to Maximum Power Charges 12% increased Critical Damage Bonus per Power Charge

beginner.whatItIs: Hunting shoes with movement speed, evasion, energy shield and intelligence that raise your maximum power charges and add critical damage for each charge held.
beginner.whyItMatters: They stack a damage bonus on top of raising the cap, so every charge you hold is worth more than it was and you can hold one more of them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical build at level thirty-three that already generates power charges reliably. Without generation the extra maximum is wasted.

name: Pragmatism
flavourText:
In an endless war against darkness,
one must be ever vigilant.
description: (200-300)% increased Armour and Evasion +(10-20)% to all Elemental Resistances +(7-13)% to Chaos Resistance Charms use no Charges

beginner.whatItIs: An explorer armour with a large defence bonus, elemental resistance and chaos resistance whose special line lets your charms be used without spending charges.
beginner.whyItMatters: Charm charges are the limit on how often you can answer an ailment, so removing the cost means the answer is always available instead of being rationed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character built around charms at level fifty-two, especially in content that applies freezes, shocks or bleeds constantly.

name: Prayers for Rain
explicitStats: 30% slower start of Energy Shield Recharge
Energy Shield Recharge is not interrupted by Damage if Recharge began Recently
flavourText:
In its final era, the roofs of Keth were rife with
anything and everything that could hold water...
should the opportunity arise.

beginner.whatItIs: A keth raiment with energy shield, intelligence and lightning resistance that starts your shield recharge more slowly but makes an ongoing recharge immune to interruption from damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: An interrupted recharge is why energy shield fails under sustained fire, so a recharge that finishes once it has started changes shield defence from unreliable to dependable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an energy shield character from level twenty-eight that fights in continuous pressure rather than short bursts.

name: Prism Guardian

flavourText: When blood is paid, the weak think twice.

beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a life-stacking character's main stat into aura capacity, so the same gear that keeps you alive also pays for another buff.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-life build at level sixty-five running reserved buffs. On a low-life character the efficiency line is small.

name: Prism of Belief

beginner.whatItIs: A diamond jewel that grants up to three levels to all skills of one randomly chosen type.
beginner.whyItMatters: Skill levels raise base damage rather than adding a percentage, so if the rolled type matches your main skill the jewel is a serious upgrade.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the skill type it rolled is the one your build actually uses. On any other roll it does nothing at all.

name: Prized Pain

explicitStats: Skills Gain 10% of Mana Cost as Extra Life Cost
(15-25)% chance to deal your Thorns Damage to Enemies you Hit with Melee Attacks
flavourText: Agony brings clarity to those of pure mind.
