beginner.whatItIs: An iron ring with strength and heavy physical thorns damage that makes your skills pay part of their mana cost in life as well, and gives a chance to deal your thorns damage on melee hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns thorns from a passive defence into an offensive stat, since the same damage now goes out when you hit rather than only when you are hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty-eight melee thorns build with recovery to cover the life cost. On a caster the added life cost is a straight risk.

name: Quatl's Molt
explicitStats: Gain Deflection Rating equal to (40-60)% of Evasion Rating
flavourText: As the serpent wills.
description: (60-80)% increased Evasion Rating +(60-80) to maximum Life +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance (10-20) Life Regeneration per second Cannot be Poisoned Gain Deflection Rating equal to (40-60)% of Evasion Rating

beginner.whatItIs: A serpentscale coat with evasion, life and life regeneration that makes you immune to poison and converts a large share of your evasion rating into deflection rating.
beginner.whyItMatters: Poison immunity removes a whole category of damage over time from the game for you, and the deflection conversion turns a stat you already stack into a second layer of defence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an evasion build from level thirty-six, and it is worth far more in chaos and poison-heavy content than the raw numbers suggest.

name: Quecholli
implicitStats: Causes Enemies to Explode on Critical kill, for 10% of their Life as Physical Damage
explicitStats: This Weapon's Critical Hit Chance is 100%
Critical Hits do not deal extra Damage
flavourText:
"The finest prosperity grows from the direst
carnage. Such is the nature of progress."
- Doryani of the Vaal
description: (100-150)% increased Physical Damage +(10-15) to all Attributes Gain 30 Life per enemy killed This Weapon's Critical Hit Chance is 100% Critical Hits do not deal extra Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A crumbling maul that always critically hits, removes the extra damage critical hits normally deal, explodes enemies killed by a critical hit, and returns life on kill.
beginner.whyItMatters: Guaranteed crits mean every effect that triggers on a critical hit fires on every swing, which is worth far more than the critical damage it gives up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level thirty-eight build with strong on-critical effects. On a build that scales critical damage it is a downgrade.

name: Queen of the Forest
explicitStats: Increases Movement Speed by 25%, plus 1% per 600 Evasion Rating, up to a maximum of 75%
Other Modifiers to Movement Speed except for Sprinting do not apply
flavourText:
Shedding away her regal past,
she forged a new destiny.
Sacrificing the ephemeral joys of man,
she embraced the eternal grasp of nature.
Seizing her one true wish,
she found peace at last.
description: (250-300)% increased Evasion Rating -(15-10)% to Fire Resistance +(25-30)% to Cold Resistance +(10-15)% to Lightning Resistance Increases Movement Speed by 25%, plus 1% per 600 Evasion Rating, up to a maximum of 75% Other Modifiers to Movement Speed except for Sprinting do not apply

beginner.whatItIs: A smuggler coat with a huge evasion bonus that converts your evasion rating into movement speed, up to seventy-five percent, while ignoring every other source of movement speed except sprinting.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes one stat pay for both defence and speed, but it also caps you: boots and passives that grant movement speed stop working entirely while it is equipped.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-evasion character at level fifty-one that stacks evasion far beyond what the tree gives. With modest evasion the coat is slower than ordinary boots.

name: Quill Rain
flavourText:
"The rain of a thousand quills that whittle
present into past, life into death."
- Rigwald of the Ezomytes
description: 100% increased Attack Speed +(10-20) to Dexterity (50-100)% increased Arrow Speed 40% less Attack Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A cheap shortbow that doubles your attack speed and increases arrow speed while dealing forty percent less attack damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades damage per hit for number of hits, so anything that triggers per hit rather than per damage, such as an on-hit effect or ailment buildup, gains enormously.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level five for levelling and for on-hit builds. It is a poor choice for a build whose damage comes from large individual hits.

name: Radiant Grief
explicitStats: Enemies in your Presence are Ignited as though dealt 200 Base Fire Damage
flavourText: No man burns alone.
description: (80-100)% increased Evasion Rating +(15-25)% to Fire Resistance 30% increased Light Radius Enemies in your Presence are Ignited as though dealt 200 Base Fire Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A lace hood with evasion, fire resistance and a wider light radius that ignites every enemy standing near you, as though they had been hit for two hundred base fire damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The ignite happens without you attacking at all, so a build that scales ignite damage gets a free application on everything that walks up to you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ignite build from level sixteen. On a build that does not scale ignites the damage stays small and the hood is only resistance.

name: Rampart Raptor
explicitStats: Bolts fired by Crossbow Attacks have 100% chance to not expend Ammunition if you've Reloaded Recently
flavourText:
"His approach to the gate was met with sounding trumpets and an unfurling of banners. He never saw it coming."
- anonymous Brotherhood of Silence report
description: (40-60)% increased Physical Damage (30-40)% increased Attack Speed Bolts fired by Crossbow Attacks have 100% chance to not expend Ammunition if you've Reloaded Recently 30% reduced Reload Speed

beginner.whatItIs: A tense crossbow with high physical damage and attack speed whose bolts stop consuming ammunition for a while after each reload, at the cost of slower reloading.
beginner.whyItMatters: Free ammunition after a reload turns the weapon's usual stop-start rhythm into a long stretch of uninterrupted fire, which is where its attack speed actually pays.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level four on a crossbow build in sustained fights. The slower reload hurts most in short bursts where you reload constantly.

name: Rathpith Globe
explicitStats: Non-Channelling Spells cost an additional 6% of your maximum Life
Non-Channelling Spells have 3% increased Critical Hit Chance per 100 maximum Life
Non-Channelling Spells deal 6% increased Damage per 100 maximum Life
flavourText:
The Vaal emptied their slaves of beating hearts,
and left a mountain of twitching dead.
description: (60-100)% increased Energy Shield +(60-100) to maximum Life Non-Channelling Spells cost an additional 6% of your maximum Life Non-Channelling Spells have 3% increased Critical Hit Chance per 100 maximum Life Non-Channelling Spells deal 6% increased Damage per 100 maximum Life

beginner.whatItIs: A sacred focus with energy shield and life that makes non-channelling spells cost a slice of your maximum life, and scales their damage and critical chance with how much life you have.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns maximum life into a spell damage stat, which makes life rolls on your gear count twice, and makes every cast a real cost you have to sustain.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-life caster at level seventy-five with strong recovery. On a low-life character the cost per cast is dangerous and the damage payoff small.

name: Rearguard
explicitStats: Adds (7-11) to (14-20) Physical Damage to Attacks
flavourText:
"It's a rare man that has eyes in the back of his head."
- Kiravi, Vaal Archer
description: Adds (7-11) to (14-20) Physical Damage to Attacks +(150-200) to Armour (20-30)% increased Projectile Speed +(15-25)% to Block chance

beginner.whatItIs: A blunt quiver with added physical damage, projectile speed, armour, stun buildup and a large chunk of block chance.
beginner.whyItMatters: Block on a quiver is unusual, and it lets a bow character get a defensive layer normally reserved for someone carrying a shield.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level thirty-three on a bow build that keeps getting caught in melee. A ranged build that never gets touched would rather have damage.

name: Redbeak
explicitStats: 100% increased Attack Damage while on Low Life
flavourText: As battle calms, blood turns to rust.
description: Adds (4-6) to (7-10) Physical Damage 10% increased Attack Speed Gain 3 Life per Enemy Killed 100% increased Attack Damage while on Low Life

beginner.whatItIs: A level one shortsword with added physical damage, attack speed and life on kill that doubles your attack damage while your life is low.
beginner.whyItMatters: It asks a new character to fight at a life total that is genuinely dangerous, and pays for it with a damage bonus nothing else offers that early.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For levelling from level one on a build that can control its life total. Without a way to sit safely at low life the bonus is rarely active.

name: Redblade Banner
explicitStats: Enemies in your Presence count as having double Power
flavourText: Blood shed is blood shared.
description: (10-15)% increased Block chance (60-100)% increased Armour +(20-30) to Strength +(100-150) to Stun Threshold Enemies in your Presence count as having double Power

beginner.whatItIs: A heraldric tower shield with block chance, armour, strength and stun threshold that makes enemies near you count as having double power.
beginner.whyItMatters: Higher enemy power feeds anything in your build that scales with it, so the shield is a deliberate buff to your opponents in service of your own mechanics.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level thirty-three build with a payoff tied to enemy power. Without one you are simply making the fight harder.

name: Redemption
explicitStats: Hits with this Weapon have no Critical Damage Bonus
Gain 1 Explosive Rhythm every (2-3) times you use a Grenade Skill
Remove all Explosive Rhythm on reaching 10 to gain Explosive Fervour for 10 Seconds
flavourText:
"The time has passed for diplomacy!
If they will not respect House Azadi,
then let them die gloriously... and loudly.
We are the masters of the Death Trades!"
- Ratha Azadi
description: (300-400)% increased Physical Damage Hits with this Weapon have no Critical Damage Bonus (40-20)% reduced Cooldown Recovery Rate Gain 1 Explosive Rhythm every (2-3) times you use a Grenade Skill Remove all Explosive Rhythm on reaching 10 to gain Explosive Fervour for 10 Seconds

beginner.whatItIs: A trarthan cannon that cannot load or fire ammunition at all, carries enormous physical damage with no critical damage bonus, and builds Explosive Rhythm as you use grenade skills until it converts into Explosive Fervour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives up the entire crossbow shooting loop to become a grenade weapon, so the build it belongs to is not a crossbow build in any usual sense.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a grenade build at level sixty-five. Equipping it on anything that fires bolts leaves you with a weapon that cannot shoot.

name: Redflare Conduit
explicitStats: 20% chance to gain a Power Charge on Hit
Lose all Power Charges on reaching maximum Power Charges
Shocks you when you reach maximum Power Charges
flavourText: In all things, control.
description: +(50-70) to maximum Mana +(20-30)% to Lightning Resistance 20% chance to gain a Power Charge on Hit Lose all Power Charges on reaching maximum Power Charges Shocks you when you reach maximum Power Charges

beginner.whatItIs: An anchorite garb with mana and lightning resistance that generates power charges on hit, then dumps all of them and shocks you the moment you reach the maximum.
beginner.whyItMatters: It creates a deliberate cycle rather than a steady buff, so your damage climbs and then resets, and the self-shock is a real cost you have to plan defences around.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that wants power charges in bursts and can either use or survive the shock, from level thirty-three.

name: Revered Resin
explicitStats: Life Flasks gain (0.17-0.25) charges per Second
flavourText: The sacred sap flows slowly, but surely.
description: +(40-60) to maximum Life (20-30)% increased Flask Life Recovery rate Life Flasks gain (0.17-0.25) charges per Second

beginner.whatItIs: An amber amulet for early characters giving strength, maximum life, faster flask healing and life flasks that fill themselves up over time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Self-filling flasks mean you stop rationing charges between packs, which is the main reason early characters back out of a fight they could have won.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear it through the campaign from level eight. Its value fades once you have gear that solves recovery in other ways.

name: Reverie
explicitStats: Non-Unique Life Flasks apply their Effects constantly
Recovery from Life Flasks cannot be Instant
Recovery from your Life Flasks cannot be applied to anything other than you
flavourText:
"Do not despair! Give yourself to the woods!
Become empty, and the Goddess will find you.
From within her roots... you shall be restored."
- Cirel of Caer Tarth
description: (100-150)% increased Armour and Energy Shield -10% to Fire Resistance +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance Cannot use Life Flasks Non-Unique Life Flasks apply their Effects constantly Recovery from Life Flasks cannot be Instant Recovery from your Life Flasks cannot be applied to anything other than you (60-40)% less Life Flask Recovery

beginner.whatItIs: A shaman mantle that stops you drinking life flasks and instead makes your ordinary life flasks apply their healing continuously, at much reduced strength.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts burst healing into constant regeneration, which is far better against steady damage over time and much worse at surviving one big hit you needed a flask for.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that dies to attrition rather than to spikes, from level twenty-eight. Give it up if your fights are decided by single dangerous hits.

name: Rise of the Phoenix
explicitStats: +25% to Fire Resistance while on Low Life
Regenerate 3% of maximum Life per second
Regenerate 3% of maximum Life per second while on Low Life
flavourText:
My bearer shall be guarded by flame,
for I am the phoenix, forever radiant in glory.
description: +5% to Maximum Fire Resistance +(20-25)% to Fire Resistance +25% to Fire Resistance while on Low Life Regenerate 3% of maximum Life per second Regenerate 3% of maximum Life per second while on Low Life

beginner.whatItIs: An omen crest shield that raises your maximum fire resistance, adds a large amount of fire resistance that grows further at low life, and regenerates a share of your life every second, doubled while low.
beginner.whyItMatters: Both halves get stronger exactly as you get closer to dying, so it is a shield built for surviving the moment rather than avoiding it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level thirty-six in fire-heavy content. Raising the maximum fire resistance is worth more than the flat resistance beside it.

name: Rite of Passage
implicitStats: Used when you kill a Rare or Unique enemy
explicitStats: Possessed by Spirit Of The (Azmeri Spirit) for (10–20) seconds on use

randomModifierPool.placeholder: Possessed by Spirit Of The (Azmeri Spirit) for (10–20) seconds on use

Possessed by Spirit Of The Boar for (10-20) seconds on use

Possessed by Spirit Of The Owl for (10-20) seconds on use

Possessed by Spirit Of The Serpent for (10-20) seconds on use
Possessed by Spirit Of The Stag for (10-20) seconds on use
Possessed by Spirit Of The Wolf for (10-20) seconds on use

flavourText:
To become a warrior and a hunter, each young
Azmeri must prove themselves before the Spirit.
description: Possessed by Spirit Of The (Azmeri Spirit) for (10–20) seconds on use

beginner.whatItIs: A golden charm that triggers when you kill a rare or unique enemy and possesses you with one of nine Azmeri animal spirits for ten to twenty seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Which spirit it rolled decides what the buff actually does, so two copies of this charm can support completely different builds.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level fifty in content dense with rare monsters, so the trigger fires often. Read the rolled spirit before building around it.

name: Rondel de Ezo
explicitStats: Curse Enemies with Enfeeble on Block
flavourText:
"Resist for long enough, and your oppressor
will lose his will. Then, you've won."
description: (50-150)% increased Evasion Rating +(10-20) to Dexterity 5 Life Regeneration per second 100% increased Block chance against Projectiles Curse Enemies with Enfeeble on Block

beginner.whatItIs: A plated buckler with evasion, dexterity and life regeneration that doubles your block chance against projectiles and curses anything you block with Enfeeble.
beginner.whyItMatters: Enfeeble weakens the enemy that just attacked you, so every successful block makes the next one less dangerous, and the projectile line covers the attacks a buckler usually struggles with.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eleven against ranged enemies. Its value drops in fights decided by a single melee slam rather than by volume of projectiles.

name: Rondel of Fragility
flavourText:
Fanatics are the most dangerous enemy,
for they care not for their own survival.
description: (15-30)% increased Skill Speed (20-30)% increased Critical Hit Chance -30% to all Elemental Resistances (30-50)% increased Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A lunar amulet that adds energy shield, critical hit chance, skill speed and a large chunk of damage, then knocks thirty points off all three elemental resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: Losing thirty resistance is not a small tax, because every point below the cap multiplies incoming elemental damage, so the amulet asks the rest of your gear to fund it before you ever equip it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it once you have enough resistance elsewhere to stay at the cap with it on. Until then, the damage gain will be paid for with deaths.

name: Runeseeker's Call
explicitStats: Only Runes can be Socketed in this item
flavourText:
Smithed from ancient metal
wrought from the very stars.
It is a means to call upon them,
for one capable of wielding it.
description: Only Runes can be Socketed in this item 200% increased effect of Socketed Runes Has 5 Augment Sockets (Hidden)

beginner.whatItIs: A runic fork with five hidden augment sockets that accepts only runes and triples their effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: The wand has no damage lines of its own, so it is a frame for runes and is worth exactly as much as the runes you put in it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level sixty-five once you own five runes worth tripling. Empty, it is one of the weakest wands you can hold.

name: Ryslatha's Coil
flavourText: All creatures have the potential for greatness or unequivocal failure.
description: +(80-100) to maximum Life (30-50)% increased Flask Life Recovery rate (30-40)% more maximum Physical Attack Damage (40-30)% less minimum Physical Attack Damage

beginner.whatItIs: An ornate belt with life and faster flask healing that raises the top end of your physical attack damage while cutting the bottom end by a similar amount.
beginner.whyItMatters: It widens the gap between your weakest and strongest hit, so your damage becomes far less predictable, with much higher peaks and much emptier misses.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slow attack build that lands few big hits, where a lucky roll matters. It is poor on a fast attacker, whose damage evens out and simply ends up mediocre.

name: Sacred Flame
explicitStats: Gain (40-60)% of Damage as Extra Fire Damage
Allies in your Presence Gain (20-30)% of Damage as Extra Fire Damage
Allies in your Presence Regenerate (2-3)% of their Maximum Life per second
Enemies in your Presence Resist Elemental Damage based on their Lowest Resistance
flavourText:
Fire destroys, but fire also purifies.
Life always springs anew.
description: Gain (40-60)% of Damage as Extra Fire Damage Allies in your Presence Gain (20-30)% of Damage as Extra Fire Damage Allies in your Presence Regenerate (2-3)% of their Maximum Life per second Enemies in your Presence Resist Elemental Damage based on their Lowest Resistance

beginner.whatItIs: A shrine sceptre that adds a large slice of fire damage for you and your allies, regenerates their life, and makes enemies near you resist elemental damage at their lowest resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forcing enemies down to their weakest resistance is a party-wide damage multiplier for every element, not only fire.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For group play at level fifty-five, and it is strongest against enemies with one badly uneven resistance.

name: Sacrosanctum
explicitStats: (10-20)% of Damage taken Recouped as Life
Damage taken Recouped as Life is also Recouped as Energy Shield
flavourText:
The Twilight Order rejected the gods, choosing
instead to put their faith in each other.
description: (80-120)% increased Armour and Energy Shield +(20-30) to Strength +(20-30) to Intelligence +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance (10-20)% of Damage taken Recouped as Life Damage taken Recouped as Life is also Recouped as Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: A corvus mantle with armour, energy shield, attributes and chaos resistance that recoups part of the damage you take as life, and applies that recoup to your energy shield as well.
beginner.whyItMatters: Recoup pays back over time regardless of what hit you, so a hybrid character gets recovery on both defensive pools from the same line without needing leech or regeneration.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-eight armour and energy shield hybrid. On a pure life build the second half of the recoup does nothing.

name: Sadist's Mercy
explicitStats: Hits with this Weapon inflict (2-5) Gruelling Madness
Enemies in your Presence have additional Power equal to their Gruelling Madness
flavourText:
"You mortals are insidious. You repress your
evil, or deny it exists. Liars! When I open
your heads, that violence floods out."
- The Raven Trickster
description: (240-300)% increased Physical Damage +(5-8)% to Critical Hit Chance (14-22)% increased Attack Speed Hits with this Weapon inflict (2-5) Gruelling Madness Enemies in your Presence have additional Power equal to their Gruelling Madness

beginner.whatItIs: A flanged mace with very high physical damage, critical chance and attack speed that stacks Gruelling Madness on hit and turns that madness into extra power for the enemies near you.
beginner.whyItMatters: You are deliberately making enemies stronger to feed something else that cares about their power, so the mace only makes sense inside a build that exploits it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-seven build with a payoff tied to enemy power. Used without one, you are simply buffing your opponents.

name: Saffell's Frame
explicitStats: Modifiers to Maximum Block Chance instead apply to Maximum Resistances
flavourText: A swift mind solves problems before they occur.
description: +(15-25)% to Fire Resistance +(15-25)% to Cold Resistance +(15-25)% to Lightning Resistance Cannot Block Modifiers to Maximum Block Chance instead apply to Maximum Resistances

beginner.whatItIs: An emblem crest shield with all three elemental resistances that cannot block at all, and instead applies your maximum block chance bonuses to your maximum resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a block build's investment into higher resistance caps, which is a stronger and more reliable defence against elemental damage than blocking is.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a build with maximum block chance modifiers to convert. Without them you have a shield that cannot block.

name: Safrin's Resolve
explicitStats: You can only Socket Ruby Jewels in this item
+(5-10)% to Cold and Lightning Resistances per Equipped Item with a Fire Resistance Modifier
flavourText:
Though the summer of centuries burns the
Vastiri to dust, we remain, unchanged.
description: Has 1 Jewel Socket (Hidden) You can only Socket Ruby Jewels in this item (10-20)% increased Rarity of Items found +(10-20) to all Attributes +(5-10)% to Cold and Lightning Resistances per Equipped Item with a Fire Resistance Modifier

beginner.whatItIs: A ring with a hidden jewel socket that only accepts ruby jewels, plus attributes, item rarity and cold and lightning resistance for each item you wear carrying a fire resistance modifier.
beginner.whyItMatters: Like its counterparts, it rewards how the rest of your gear is rolled, so it is strongest on a character whose items already share a resistance theme.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty when several pieces already carry fire resistance and you own a ruby jewel worth the socket.

name: Saitha's Spear
implicitStats: Bleeding you inflict deals Damage (10-20)% faster
explicitStats: (15-25)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit
Aggravating any Bleeding with this Weapon also Aggravates all Ignites on the target
(25-40)% chance to Aggravate Bleeding on Hit
flavourText:
Born in a star of man's own make,
fused to her hand by her last mistake.
description: Adds (14-26) to (27-32) Physical Damage Adds (33-41) to (47-53) Fire Damage (15-25)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit Aggravating any Bleeding with this Weapon also Aggravates all Ignites on the target (25-40)% chance to Aggravate Bleeding on Hit

beginner.whatItIs: A barbed spear with added physical and fire damage that causes and aggravates bleeding, and makes aggravating a bleed with it also aggravate every ignite on the target.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links bleed and ignite so one action keeps both damage over time effects ticking at full rate, which normally takes two separate mechanics.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level thirty-three build that both bleeds and ignites. With only one of the two, half the weapon is idle.

name: Sands of Silk
flavourText: The desert is ever flowing.
description: (50-100)% increased Evasion Rating +(50-80) to maximum Mana +(10-20) to Dexterity +(10-20) to Intelligence +(10-15)% to Fire Resistance (15-30)% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate

beginner.whatItIs: A shrouded vest with evasion, mana, attributes and fire resistance that speeds up how quickly your cooldowns come back.
beginner.whyItMatters: Cooldown recovery is normally hard to find outside of specific slots, and putting it on a chest lets a build that leans on a cooldown skill use it noticeably more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on any character whose main damage or defence sits behind a cooldown. It is a plain evasion chest for anyone else.

name: Sandstorm Visage
explicitStats: Enemies in your Presence are Blinded
Every second, inflicts Critical Weakness on enemies in your Presence for (15-20) seconds
flavourText: A fell wind brings death.
description: +(80-120) to maximum Energy Shield +(20-30) to Dexterity Enemies in your Presence are Blinded Every second, inflicts Critical Weakness on enemies in your Presence for (15-20) seconds

beginner.whatItIs: A chain tiara with energy shield and dexterity that blinds every enemy near you and stacks Critical Weakness on them once a second.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blind lowers their chance to hit you while Critical Weakness raises your chance to crit them, so one helmet handles both halves of a fight passively.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical build at level fifty-two that fights at close range, since both effects only reach enemies inside your presence.

name: Sanguine Diviner
explicitStats: 25% chance to inflict Bleeding on Hit
25% of Spell Mana Cost Converted to Life Cost
flavourText: One way or another, it will find what it seeks.
description: (80-100)% increased Spell Damage Gain (10-15) Life per enemy killed 25% chance to inflict Bleeding on Hit 25% of Spell Mana Cost Converted to Life Cost

beginner.whatItIs: A bone wand available at level two with a large spell damage bonus and life on kill that converts a quarter of your spell mana costs into life costs and bleeds enemies on hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Paying part of every cast in life is a real risk on a low-level caster, and the life on kill is what makes it survivable while you are clearing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level two on a caster with a decent life pool. In a long fight with nothing dying, the life cost has nothing paying it back.

name: Sanguis Heroum
flavourText:
Wraeclast has known too few true heroes.
It remembers those that stood in defiance.
description: Creates Consecrated Ground on use Gains (0.15-0.20) Charges per Second

beginner.whatItIs: A staunching charm that triggers when you start bleeding, creates consecrated ground under you, and refills its own charges over time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Consecrated ground heals and steadies you where you are standing, so a bleed you would normally have to run from becomes a moment of recovery instead.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eighteen against enemies that inflict bleeding, particularly on a melee character that cannot easily disengage.

name: Scold's Bridle
explicitStats: Take (25-100)% of Mana Costs you pay for Skills as Physical Damage
flavourText:
"The sharper the pain, the sharper the mind.
A curious paradox."
- Shavronne of Umbra
description: +(75-150) to maximum Energy Shield (60-100)% increased Spell Damage +(80-100) to maximum Mana 15% reduced Cast Speed Take (25-100)% of Mana Costs you pay for Skills as Physical Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A jade tiara with a large energy shield, mana and spell damage bonus that deals you physical damage equal to a share of every mana cost you pay, and slows your casting.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes casting hurt you on purpose, which is a real damage source for builds that trigger effects when you take damage, and a slow suicide for everything else.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty caster built around self-damage, with the recovery to survive it. Read the roll carefully, since the self-damage ranges from a quarter to the whole cost.

name: Sculpted Suffering
explicitStats: Breaks Armour equal to 40% of damage from Hits with this weapon
Fully Armour Broken enemies you kill with Hits Shatter
flavourText:
The Abyssals were created, not born,
and every moment in the light was agony.
description: Adds (21-26) to (25-31) Physical Damage (10-15)% increased Attack Speed Breaks Armour equal to 40% of damage from Hits with this weapon Fully Armour Broken enemies you kill with Hits Shatter

beginner.whatItIs: A warpick with added physical damage, attack speed and extra critical damage that breaks armour equal to a large share of its damage, and shatters fully armour-broken enemies you kill.
beginner.whyItMatters: Breaking armour makes every later hit land harder, so the weapon sets up its own damage and then removes the corpses of what it kills.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-two against armoured enemies, where the armour break matters most. Against unarmoured monsters half the weapon is idle.

name: Season of the Hunt
implicitStats: Empowers the Map Boss of a Map
explicitStats: Map Bosses are Hunted by Azmeri Spirits
flavourText:
Darkness and light, naught but forest between.
As the forest fades, the twilight hunt begins.
description: Map Bosses are Hunted by Azmeri Spirits

beginner.whatItIs: An overseer tablet with five uses that makes map bosses hunted by Azmeri spirits.
beginner.whyItMatters: It changes the shape of the boss encounter rather than only its numbers, adding another party to the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On maps where you want the additional encounter. Its value depends on how much you get out of the spirits themselves.

name: Seed of Cataclysm
explicitStats: (30-50)% increased Critical Hit Chance for Spells
5% reduced Critical Spell Damage Bonus per Critical Hit you've dealt with Spells Recently
(15-30)% chance for Spell Damage with Critical Hits to be Lucky
flavourText: The dawn of a new era is set into motion
description: (30-50)% increased Critical Hit Chance for Spells 5% reduced Critical Spell Damage Bonus per Critical Hit you've dealt with Spells Recently +(13-17)% to Chaos Resistance 10% increased Mana Cost of Skills (15-30)% chance for Spell Damage with Critical Hits to be Lucky

beginner.whatItIs: A lazuli ring with chaos resistance and a large spell critical chance bonus that reduces your critical spell damage for each recent spell critical hit, and gives a chance for critical spell damage to be lucky.
beginner.whyItMatters: Critting often makes your later crits smaller, so the ring rewards big occasional critical spells rather than a continuous stream of them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on a slow, hard-hitting critical caster. On a rapid-fire spell build the penalty compounds constantly.

name: Seeing Stars
flavourText: Within lies a window.
description: Adds (12-16) to (22-25) Cold Damage Adds 1 to (40-45) Lightning Damage (10-20)% increased Attack Speed Energy Generation is doubled

beginner.whatItIs: A marching mace with added cold and lightning damage and extra attack speed whose special line doubles the rate you generate energy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Energy is what pays for triggered skills, so doubling generation means the skills you have set to fire automatically go off roughly twice as often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty-four build using trigger skills. On a build with nothing to spend energy on the line is wasted.

name: Serle's Grit
explicitStats: Skills which Empower an Attack have (10-20)% chance to not count that Attack
(40-50) to (80-100) added Physical Thorns damage per Runic Plate
flavourText:
A common soldier from a common family kept hammering into the night
after each grueling march, his eyes afire with starlight and determination.
Few suspected that he would one day become the greatest among them.
description: Maximum Quality is 40% Adds (23-30) to (35-55) Physical Damage +(20-30) to Strength Skills which Empower an Attack have (10-20)% chance to not count that Attack (40-50) to (80-100) added Physical Thorns damage per Runic Plate

beginner.whatItIs: A kalguuran forgehammer with three sockets, added physical damage and strength that deals physical thorns damage for each runic plate you have, and sometimes lets an empowered attack not be counted as spent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Not consuming an empowerment means the buff carries into another attack, so a build that empowers gets extra hits out of the same setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty-seven build using empowered attacks and runic plates. Without plates the thorns line contributes nothing.

name: Serpent's Egg
explicitStats: Gain an additional Charge when you gain a Charge
flavourText:
When Kabala the Serpent Queen was banished from Keth,
the Sekhemas took a single hostage as punishment.
description: +(10-20) to all Attributes +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance (20-30)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Gain an additional Charge when you gain a Charge

beginner.whatItIs: A gold amulet with attributes, chaos resistance, mana regeneration and item rarity whose special line gives you a second charge every time you gain one.
beginner.whyItMatters: Power, frenzy and endurance charges are hard to keep stacked at full, and doubling the rate you gain them means you spend far more of a fight at maximum charges.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any build whose damage or defence is built on charges. If nothing you run generates them, the special line is dead weight.

name: Serpent's Lesson
explicitStats: You count as on Low Life while at 35% of maximum Mana or below
You count as on Low Mana while at 35% of maximum Life or below
flavourText: Sinuous, entwined... inextricable.
description: +(60-100) to maximum Life +(60-100) to maximum Mana You count as on Low Life while at 35% of maximum Mana or below You count as on Low Mana while at 35% of maximum Life or below

beginner.whatItIs: A tonal focus with a large life and mana boost whose special lines make low mana count as low life and low life count as low mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many effects trigger on low life or low mana, and swapping the two conditions lets a build reach those triggers safely through the resource it can afford to spend.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with low life or low mana triggers, from level twenty-two. Without any such trigger the focus is only its life and mana rolls.

name: Shackles of the Wretched
explicitStats: You cannot be Chilled for 6 seconds after being Chilled
You cannot be Frozen for 6 seconds after being Frozen
You cannot be Ignited for 6 seconds after being Ignited
You cannot be Shocked for 6 seconds after being Shocked
Curses you inflict are reflected back to you
flavourText: Captivity breeds creativity.
description: (30-50)% increased Armour and Energy Shield You cannot be Chilled for 6 seconds after being Chilled You cannot be Frozen for 6 seconds after being Frozen You cannot be Ignited for 6 seconds after being Ignited You cannot be Shocked for 6 seconds after being Shocked Curses you inflict are reflected back to you

beginner.whatItIs: Aged cuffs with armour and energy shield that give you six seconds of immunity after each chill, freeze, ignite or shock, and reflect every curse you cast back onto yourself.
beginner.whyItMatters: The immunity windows mean an ailment can only land on you once in a while instead of continuously, but the reflected curses make cursing an act of self-harm.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a build that casts no curses, in content that layers ailments. On a curse build the reflection is a serious downside.

name: Shankgonne
explicitStats: Gain Deflection Rating equal to 20% of Armour
flavourText:
"Captain Hiff Greybeard accomplished what nary a Brinerot
could: he died of old age. Almost had him a dozen times
meself, if it weren't for that damn leg of his... crafty shite..."
description: (80-100)% increased Armour and Evasion (10-20)% increased Rarity of Items found +(15-25)% to Fire Resistance Gain Deflection Rating equal to 20% of Armour +(200-300) to Stun Threshold You cannot Sprint Cannon Ball Footsteps (Hidden)

beginner.whatItIs: Covered sabatons with armour, evasion, fire resistance and item rarity that convert a fifth of your armour into deflection rating and stop you sprinting entirely.
beginner.whyItMatters: Losing sprint is a permanent mobility cut, so the boots are asking you to pay in movement for a defensive layer armour cannot give you on its own.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavily armoured, slow character at level forty-six that never relied on sprinting. On anything mobile the cost is far too high.

name: Shavronne's Satchel
explicitStats: Life Recovery from Flasks also applies to Energy Shield
flavourText: Bring mystery to life. Again and again.
description: (30-20)% reduced Flask Life Recovery rate +(20-30) to Intelligence (20-30)% increased Flask Charges gained Life Recovery from Flasks also applies to Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: A fine belt with intelligence and extra flask charges that makes flask life recovery refill your energy shield as well, while reducing how much life those flasks restore.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives an energy shield character something it normally cannot have at all, which is an instant recovery button under its own control instead of waiting for the recharge delay.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an energy shield build from level sixty-two. On a life-based character the reduced recovery rate is a straight downgrade.

name: Shyaba
flavourText: Be not deceived by the treachery of men.
description: +50 Dexterity Requirement -15 Strength Requirement (80-120)% increased Physical Damage 50% increased Attack Speed (15-25)% increased Light Radius Always Hits

beginner.whatItIs: A temple maul with a large physical damage bonus and a huge attack speed increase that always hits, and asks for dexterity instead of some of its strength.
beginner.whyItMatters: Never missing removes accuracy from your gear budget entirely, which is normally a real cost on a two-handed attack build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-eight on a mace build short of accuracy. Note the unusual dexterity requirement before planning attributes.

name: Sierran Inheritance
explicitStats: All Damage taken from Hits Contributes to Magnitude of Chill inflicted on you
The Effect of Chill on you is reversed
flavourText:
Born among the high peaks, many Mutewind
live their entire lives in snow and ice.
description: (50-80)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield -15% to Cold Resistance +(30-40)% to Lightning Resistance (15-30)% increased Energy Shield Recharge Rate All Damage taken from Hits Contributes to Magnitude of Chill inflicted on you The Effect of Chill on you is reversed

beginner.whatItIs: A marabout garb with evasion, energy shield and heavy lightning resistance that reverses the effect of chill on you, while making every hit you take contribute to chilling you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reversed chill means being chilled speeds you up instead of slowing you down, so a debuff you normally fight to avoid becomes something you want applied constantly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen, and it is strongest in cold-heavy content where you will be chilled anyway. The lowered cold resistance is the price of that.

name: Silks of Veneration
explicitStats: Current Energy Shield also grants Elemental Damage reduction
flavourText:
Hallowed Dordalus was cast into the pit as a heretic,
but his piety was so great, he would not burn.
He rose again, lauded, his faith forever changed...
but not the way the Templar believed.
description: (150-200)% increased Energy Shield +(30-50) to Spirit +(20-30) to Intelligence (30-50)% increased Energy Shield Recharge Rate Current Energy Shield also grants Elemental Damage reduction

beginner.whatItIs: An enlightened robe with a very large energy shield pool, spirit, intelligence and faster recharge, whose special line makes your current energy shield reduce elemental damage taken.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts the size of your shield into a permanent damage reduction, so stacking shield stops being only a bigger buffer and starts making every elemental hit smaller.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a dedicated energy shield caster at level sixty-eight with a high shield pool. With a small pool the reduction is barely noticeable.

name: Silverthorne
explicitStats: Parrying applies 10 Stacks of Critical Weakness
flavourText:
As a boy, in the arena, Daresso learned to
feign weakness to open up a lethal blow.
description: (60-100)% increased Evasion Rating +(10-15)% to all Elemental Resistances Parrying applies 10 Stacks of Critical Weakness 100% increased Parry Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A spiked buckler with evasion and elemental resistance that doubles your parry damage and stacks ten Critical Weakness on anything you parry.
beginner.whyItMatters: Critical Weakness makes the target far easier to critically hit, so parrying becomes the opener that sets up your damage rather than a purely defensive reaction.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical melee build at level twenty-six that parries on purpose. A build that never parries gets none of it.

name: Sine Aequo
explicitStats: (150-200)% increased Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield
Immobilise enemies at 50% buildup instead of 100%
flavourText: The greatest warrior of his era fought with honour.
description: (10-15)% increased Skill Speed (150-200)% increased Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield Immobilise enemies at 50% buildup instead of 100% (30-50)% increased Damage against Immobilised Enemies

beginner.whatItIs: Grand manchettes with skill speed and very high defences that immobilise enemies at half the usual buildup and increase your damage against immobilised targets.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reaching immobilisation twice as easily means the crowd control lands during the fight rather than after it, and the damage bonus turns that control into a kill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five build that already applies immobilisation buildup, particularly against rare and boss monsters that resist it.

name: Sire of Shards
explicitStats: Spells fire Projectiles in a circle
flavourText: That which was broken may yet break.
description: (80-120)% increased Spell Damage (10-20)% increased Cast Speed +(5-10)% to all Elemental Resistances 20% increased Light Radius Spells fire 4 additional Projectiles Spells fire Projectiles in a circle

beginner.whatItIs: A chiming staff with spell damage, cast speed and elemental resistance that makes your spells fire four extra projectiles, spread out in a full circle.
beginner.whyItMatters: Firing in a circle means your spells cover every direction rather than the one you aimed at, which changes how a projectile caster positions entirely.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-five on a projectile spell build clearing packs. Against a single target most of the circle misses.

name: Skin of the Loyal
explicitStats: Elemental Ailment Threshold is increased by Uncapped Chaos Resistance
Armour is increased by Uncapped Fire Resistance
Energy Shield is increased by Uncapped Cold Resistance
Evasion Rating is increased by Uncapped Lightning Resistance
flavourText:
We happily give our limbs.
A net woven to keep safe the bones of the Lords.
description: +(5-40)% to all Elemental Resistances Elemental Ailment Threshold is increased by Uncapped Chaos Resistance Armour is increased by Uncapped Fire Resistance Energy Shield is increased by Uncapped Cold Resistance Evasion Rating is increased by Uncapped Lightning Resistance

beginner.whatItIs: A level one garment with elemental resistance that turns each of your uncapped resistances into a defence: fire into armour, cold into energy shield, lightning into evasion, and chaos into ailment threshold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Resistance above the cap is normally wasted, so this makes overcapping a deliberate way to buy defences instead of an insurance policy against having them stripped.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character that deliberately stacks resistance far past the cap. On a build sitting exactly at the cap the garment gives almost nothing.

name: Skysliver
explicitStats: Rolls only the minimum or maximum Damage value for each Damage Type
flavourText: Heads fall to the sand, just as the star fell from the sky
description: No Physical Damage Adds 1 to (80-120) Lightning Damage (15-30)% increased Attack Speed (50-100)% increased chance to Shock Rolls only the minimum or maximum Damage value for each Damage Type

beginner.whatItIs: A winged spear with no physical damage, an enormous lightning damage range, extra attack speed, a much higher shock chance, and a line that makes it roll only the lowest or the highest damage value.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the middle of the damage range means every hit is either near-nothing or near-maximum, so your damage is far swingier than the average suggests.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a lightning build that wants shocks and can absorb a bad streak of low rolls.

name: Slivertongue
explicitStats: Leeches (5-8)% of Physical Damage as Life
Leeches (4-7)% of Physical Damage as Mana
Arrows Pierce all targets after Forking
flavourText: A hundred blind heads, each seeking the taste of prey on the air.
description: Adds (40-48) to (65-72) Physical Damage +(4-6)% to Critical Hit Chance Leeches (5-8)% of Physical Damage as Life Leeches (4-7)% of Physical Damage as Mana Arrows Fork Arrows Pierce all targets after Forking

beginner.whatItIs: A zealot bow with large added physical damage, critical hit chance and both life and mana leech, whose arrows fork and then pierce everything after forking.
beginner.whyItMatters: Fork followed by pierce means a single arrow keeps hitting long after its first target, which multiplies your clear speed without adding any attack speed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical bow build from level thirty-nine clearing packs. Against a single boss the fork line adds very little.

name: Snakebite
explicitStats: Targets can be affected by +1 of your Poisons at the same time
flavourText:
As the serpent shuns thought,
It shuns fear.
It strikes with the speed of wrath
And the skill of compulsion.
description: (40-60)% increased Evasion Rating +(7-17)% to Chaos Resistance (6-10) Life Regeneration per second (20-30)% chance to Poison on Hit Targets can be affected by +1 of your Poisons at the same time

beginner.whatItIs: Spined bracers with evasion, chaos resistance and life regeneration that give a chance to poison on hit and let one extra of your poisons stack on a target at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: Poison damage is decided by how many stacks a target carries, so raising the stack limit is a direct multiplier on a poison build's damage against a single enemy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build at level thirty-three fighting bosses, where stacks have time to build up.

name: Snakepit
explicitStats: Left ring slot: Projectiles from Spells cannot Chain
Left ring slot: Projectiles from Spells Fork
Right ring slot: Projectiles from Spells Chain +1 times
Right ring slot: Projectiles from Spells cannot Fork
flavourText: They wrap around you until your blood turns as cold as theirs.
description: (20-30)% increased Spell Damage (10-15)% increased Cast Speed Left ring slot: Projectiles from Spells cannot Chain Left ring slot: Projectiles from Spells Fork Right ring slot: Projectiles from Spells Chain +1 times Right ring slot: Projectiles from Spells cannot Fork Projectiles from Spells cannot Pierce

beginner.whatItIs: A pearl ring with spell damage and cast speed that changes how your spell projectiles behave depending on which hand it is worn on, forking in the left slot and chaining in the right, and never piercing either way.
beginner.whyItMatters: The same ring is two different items depending on the slot, so where you wear it is a real build decision rather than a formality.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level thirty-two on a spell projectile build, in the slot that matches how you want your projectiles to spread.

name: Solus Ipse
explicitStats: (150-200)% increased Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield
Equipment and Skill Gems have 25% increased Attribute Requirements
You can Socket 2 additional copies of each Lineage Support Gem, in different Skills
flavourText: One warrior alone survived to face the Arbiter.
description: +(60-100) to maximum Mana 25% increased Light Radius (150-200)% increased Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield Equipment and Skill Gems have 25% increased Attribute Requirements You can Socket 2 additional copies of each Lineage Support Gem, in different Skills

beginner.whatItIs: A grand visage with mana and high defences that lets you socket two extra copies of each Lineage support gem in different skills, in exchange for steeper attribute requirements on everything you wear and use.
beginner.whyItMatters: Support gems are normally limited to one copy across your whole character, so the helmet unlocks combinations of supports that are otherwise impossible.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five build using Lineage supports it wants on several skills at once. The raised requirements affect every slot, so plan attributes first.

name: Soul Mantle
explicitStats: +1 to maximum number of Summoned Totems
Inflicts a random Curse on you when your Totems die, ignoring Curse limit
flavourText:
The greatest mistakes cause suffering
long after they have been made
description: (80-120)% increased Armour and Energy Shield +75 to Spirit +10 to Strength +15 to Intelligence +1 to maximum number of Summoned Totems Inflicts a random Curse on you when your Totems die, ignoring Curse limit

beginner.whatItIs: A sacrificial mantle with seventy-five spirit and an extra totem that curses you at random, ignoring the usual curse limit, every time one of your totems dies.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra totem is a straight damage increase, but the curses stack up as your totems are destroyed, so the chest gets more dangerous exactly as a fight goes badly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a totem build from level thirty-six that can keep its totems alive or remove curses. Without an answer to the curses it turns hard fights into deaths.

name: Soul Tether
explicitStats: You lose 5% of maximum Energy Shield per second
Excess Life Recovery from Leech is applied to Energy Shield
flavourText:
Vaal bloodpriests were among the earliest intellectuals on record.
It was they who found that a newly freed soul would
desperately cling to any other source of life.
description: +(40-60) to maximum Energy Shield +(20-30) to Intelligence You lose 5% of maximum Energy Shield per second Excess Life Recovery from Leech is applied to Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: A long belt with energy shield and intelligence that drains five percent of your shield every second and redirects any life leech you cannot use into that shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: The drain never stops, so the belt is only survivable on a character that is leeching constantly, and it punishes any pause in combat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it on a leech-based attack build with a full life pool from level twenty. It is dangerous on anything that stops hitting for more than a few seconds.

name: Spire of Ire
explicitStats: Leeches (10-20)% of Physical Damage as Life
When you Consume a Charge Trigger Chaotic Surge to gain 2 Chaos Surges
Life Leech recovers based on your Chaos damage instead of Physical damage
flavourText:
The spear was specially forged to assassinate Voll,
but Maligaro never got a chance to use it...
description: (15-20)% increased Attack Speed Leeches (10-20)% of Physical Damage as Life Adds (167-201) to (267-333) Chaos damage When you Consume a Charge Trigger Chaotic Surge to gain 2 Chaos Surges Life Leech recovers based on your Chaos damage instead of Physical damage

beginner.whatItIs: A helix spear with huge added chaos damage and attack speed whose leech recovers based on your chaos damage instead of your physical damage, and which triggers Chaotic Surge when you consume a charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: Leech normally only comes from physical damage, so redirecting it to chaos is what lets a chaos build sustain itself at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five chaos build that consumes charges. On a physical build the leech line takes away your recovery.

name: Spiteful Floret
explicitStats: (20-30)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit
Every 5 Rage also grants 5% of Damage taken Recouped as Life
flavourText:
If you see the blushing tree of the northern woods,
remember: "Blossoms of red, the tree's been fed.
Blossoms of white, prepare for a fight."
description: (60-90)% increased Physical Damage (6-10)% increased Attack Speed +(7-14) to Strength (20-30)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit Every 5 Rage also grants 5% of Damage taken Recouped as Life

beginner.whatItIs: A nettle talisman with physical damage, attack speed and strength that causes bleeding on hit and recoups a share of the damage you take as life for every five rage you hold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rage becomes a defensive stat as well as an offensive one, so a build that keeps its bar full is quietly healing from every hit it takes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level five on a rage build. Without rage generation the recoup line contributes nothing.

name: Splinter of Lorrata
explicitStats: 20% increased Melee Strike Range with this weapon
Any number of Poisons from this Weapon can affect a target at the same time
Always Poison on Hit with this weapon
flavourText: The Baleful Gem's corruption lingers still...
description: Adds (2-3) to (6-8) Physical Damage Deal no Elemental Damage 20% increased Melee Strike Range with this weapon Any number of Poisons from this Weapon can affect a target at the same time Always Poison on Hit with this weapon

beginner.whatItIs: A level one hardwood spear that always poisons on hit, lets any number of its poisons stack on one target, extends your strike range, and deals no elemental damage at all.
beginner.whyItMatters: Unlimited poison stacking is normally the ceiling on a poison build's single-target damage, and this removes it from a level one weapon.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one for a poison build, especially against a boss where stacks have time to pile up. Any elemental scaling you have is switched off.

name: Splinterheart
flavourText:
The forests of the Vastiri held many secrets
mystical and dark. Men learned not to wander,
lest they return with a strange new purpose.
description: (120-160)% increased Physical Damage +(50-70) to Accuracy Rating (20-30)% increased Projectile Speed Projectiles Split towards +2 targets

beginner.whatItIs: A recurve bow with high physical damage, accuracy and projectile speed whose projectiles split towards two extra targets.
beginner.whyItMatters: Splitting sends damage at enemies you did not aim at, so a simple attack covers a group, which matters most in the early acts where clear speed is slow.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an early bow character from level sixteen clearing packs. Splitting is wasted when only one enemy is on screen.

name: Split Personality
explicitStats: Can Allocate Passive Skills from the (Random class) starting point

Can Allocate Passive Skills from the Shadow's starting point

flavourText:
"Try on another life. See how it fits. You'll
find that your one life is utterly inadequate."
- He of Many Names and Many Faces
description: Can Allocate Passive Skills from the (Random class) starting point

beginner.whatItIs: A ruby jewel that lets you allocate passive skills starting from another class's starting point on the tree.
beginner.whyItMatters: It opens a part of the tree your class would need a long walk to reach, so a build can borrow a whole cluster from a different starting area.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the rolled class starting point is near passives your build wants. Which class it rolled decides whether it is useful.

name: Starkonja's Head
explicitStats: 150% increased Global Evasion Rating when on Low Life
15% of Damage from Hits is taken from your Damageable Companion's Life before you
flavourText:
There was no hero made out of Starkonja's death,
but merely a long sleep made eternal.
description: (100-200)% increased Evasion Rating (15-25)% increased Critical Hit Chance +(30-40) to Dexterity 150% increased Global Evasion Rating when on Low Life 15% of Damage from Hits is taken from your Damageable Companion's Life before you

beginner.whatItIs: A leatherbound hood with heavy evasion, critical hit chance and dexterity that greatly increases your evasion while your life is low, and pushes part of every hit onto your companion first.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its defences arrive exactly when you are about to die, and the companion soaks a share of the damage on the way, so both lines cover the same emergency.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an evasion build with a companion at level fifty. Without a companion you lose the damage sharing and keep only the low-life evasion.

name: Stone of Lazhwar
explicitStats: +(15-25)% to Block Chance while holding a Focus
flavourText:
You are slow, foolish and ignorant.
I am not.
description: +(50-100) to maximum Mana (15-25)% increased Cast Speed +(15-25)% to Block Chance while holding a Focus

beginner.whatItIs: An early lapis amulet with intelligence, extra mana and cast speed, plus a big chunk of block chance while you are holding a focus.
beginner.whyItMatters: Block on a caster is unusual, and the amulet supplies enough of it that a focus-holding spellcaster can stand in a fight instead of retreating from every melee monster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eight on any caster committed to a focus in the off-hand. Swapping to a shield or a two-handed weapon throws the block line away.

name: Strugglescream
flavourText:
There is no light at the end of this inner strife,
but the shadows eventually become home.
description: Can have 3 additional Instilled Modifiers

beginner.whatItIs: A stellar amulet whose only line lets the item carry three more instilled modifiers than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Instilled modifiers are the ones you add yourself, so the amulet is deliberately close to blank on the shelf and becomes whatever your build needs once you have filled it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it up when you already have the currency to fill the extra slots. Worn unfilled it is one of the weakest amulets you can equip.

name: Sunsplinter
explicitStats: +(1–3) to Level of all Fire Skills +(1–3) to Level of all Cold Skills +(1–3) to Level of all Lightning Skills +(1-3)% to Maximum Fire Resistance +(1-3)% to Maximum Cold Resistance +(1-3)% to Maximum Lightning Resistance
