flavourText:
"Lundara held back the hordes, while Solerai rose to split the sky.
With a single stroke, she ended the Winter of the World."
- Wranga, tale-woman of the Wahida akhara
description: (100-300)% increased Evasion Rating +(1–3) to Level of all Fire Skills +(1–3) to Level of all Cold Skills +(1–3) to Level of all Lightning Skills +(1-3)% to Maximum Fire Resistance +(1-3)% to Maximum Cold Resistance +(1-3)% to Maximum Lightning Resistance

beginner.whatItIs: An array buckler with a very large evasion bonus that rolls levels on your fire, cold and lightning skills, or extra maximum resistance to each of those three elements.
beginner.whyItMatters: The two possible outcomes are completely different items, one offensive and one defensive, so which Sunsplinter you found matters far more than the item's name.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level fifty-five, matched to the roll you actually have. Read the three lines before planning a build around it.

name: Surefooted Sigil
explicitStats: 50% increased Evasion Rating if you've Dodge Rolled Recently
flavourText: Natural grace is born, not earned.
description: +(40-60) to maximum Life +(5-15) to Dexterity +1 metre to Dodge Roll distance 50% increased Evasion Rating if you've Dodge Rolled Recently

beginner.whatItIs: A jade amulet with life and dexterity that adds a metre to how far your dodge roll travels and boosts evasion for a moment after you roll.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra metre is the difference between rolling to the edge of an attack and rolling clear of it, which matters most in the campaign where you have no other way to avoid a slam.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Wear it from level eight on any character that relies on rolling out of danger, and keep it as long as nothing better replaces the life.

name: Surge of the Tide
explicitStats: Every second Slam Skill you use while Shapeshifted is Ancestrally Boosted
Every second Strike Skill you use while Shapeshifted is Ancestrally Boosted
flavourText:
"A traditional hatungo does not carry an axe,
it is true. But as Narumoa showed us, there
are many ways to crush one's enemy..."
description: (250-300)% increased Physical Damage (30-50)% increased Armour (15-10)% reduced Attack Speed +(20-30) to Strength Every second Slam Skill you use while Shapeshifted is Ancestrally Boosted Every second Strike Skill you use while Shapeshifted is Ancestrally Boosted

beginner.whatItIs: A lumbering talisman with very high physical damage and armour that ancestrally boosts every second slam and every second strike skill you use while shapeshifted.
beginner.whyItMatters: Alternating boosted hits gives a slow, heavy build a rhythm where every other attack lands much harder, which suits its low attack speed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty-two shapeshifting melee build. Outside animal form the boosting lines never trigger.

name: Svalinn
explicitStats: Chance to Block Damage is Lucky
You take (0-20)% of damage from Blocked Hits
flavourText:
The priests found the Great Shield the night it fell to Middengard,
but it was the smiths who delved into the secrets it held.
description: +(50-100) to maximum Runic Ward (200-300)% increased Armour Chance to Block Damage is Lucky You take (0-20)% of damage from Blocked Hits

beginner.whatItIs: A crucible tower shield with runic ward and very high armour that makes your chance to block lucky and can reduce the damage from blocked hits to nothing.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lucky block rolls twice and keeps the better result, which raises your effective block far beyond the number printed on your character sheet.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty block build, and check the damage-through roll, since it ranges from a perfect block to a fifth getting through.

name: Sylvan's Effigy
explicitStats: Allies in your Presence Regenerate (50-100) Life per second
Companions deal (50-100)% increased damage to your Marked targets
You can have any number of Companions of different types
flavourText:
Darkness howls through ancient bones, a wistful cry
on hollow winds. The moon listens. The pack gathers.
description: (50-75)% increased Spirit Allies in your Presence Regenerate (50-100) Life per second +(6-12) to all Attributes Companions deal (50-100)% increased damage to your Marked targets You can have any number of Companions of different types

beginner.whatItIs: A stoic sceptre with a large spirit bonus and attributes that regenerates allies' life, boosts companion damage against your marked targets, and lets you keep any number of companions of different types.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the limit on how many companion types you can field is a structural change to a companion build rather than a numerical one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a companion build at level sixty-two with the spirit to support several of them at once.

name: Tabula Rasa
description: Has 6 Jewel Sockets (Hidden)

beginner.whatItIs: A plain level one garment with no stats at all and six hidden jewel sockets.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives up every defence on the chest slot in exchange for six jewels, so the value is entirely in the jewels you own rather than in the item itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For levelling and for testing builds, where six cheap jewels beat the small defences a low-level chest offers. Replace it before content that can kill you.

name: Tangletongue
explicitStats: 10% of Skill Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs
flavourText:
"In the hands of Orbala, it made a god bleed."
- Wranga, tale-woman of the Wahida akhara
description: Adds (14-18) to (30-36) Physical Damage +(5-8)% to Critical Hit Chance +(15-25) to Intelligence Bifurcates Critical Hits 10% of Skill Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs

beginner.whatItIs: A forked spear with added physical damage, critical hit chance and intelligence that bifurcates your critical hits and converts part of your mana costs into life costs.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bifurcating a critical hit splits it into two projectiles, so critting becomes a clear speed mechanic as well as a damage one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical spear build at level twenty-six with the recovery to cover the life cost on every skill.

name: Taryn's Shiver
explicitStats: Enemies Frozen by you take 100% increased Damage
flavourText:
Shed by the winged beast of night,
A scaly frost-encrusted thorn.
All who feel its wintry light
Shiver in pain at the frozen dawn.
description: (80-120)% increased Spell Damage (10-20)% increased Cast Speed 30% increased Freeze Buildup Enemies Frozen by you take 100% increased Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A gelid staff with spell damage, cast speed and faster freeze buildup that makes enemies you have frozen take double damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Freezing is already defensive, and doubling the damage on frozen targets makes it your damage setup as well, so one action does both jobs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level two on a cold caster. Against bosses that resist freeze the damage bonus rarely applies.

name: Temporalis
explicitStats: (5-30)% of Damage taken Recouped as Life
(5-30)% of Damage taken Recouped as Mana
flavourText:
The final element the tale-women
mastered was Time itself.
description: +(100-150) to maximum Energy Shield +(10-20)% to all Elemental Resistances (5-30)% of Damage taken Recouped as Life (5-30)% of Damage taken Recouped as Mana Skills have -(2-1) seconds to Cooldown

beginner.whatItIs: A silk robe with energy shield and resistances that recoups part of the damage you take as both life and mana, and cuts one to two seconds off every skill cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: A flat cooldown reduction affects short cooldowns most, so skills that were used occasionally can end up available almost constantly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-four build whose skills sit on short cooldowns. On skills with long cooldowns two seconds barely registers.

name: Tetzlapokal's Desire
flavourText: A faith born of flesh.
description: (100-150)% increased Energy Shield +(20-30) to Strength +(20-30) to Intelligence +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance Life Recharges

beginner.whatItIs: A votive raiment with energy shield, attributes and chaos resistance whose special line makes your life recharge the way energy shield normally does.
beginner.whyItMatters: Life recovery is usually flasks and regeneration, so giving life a recharge means it refills itself completely after a break in combat with no resource spent.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a life-based character from level thirty-three that can disengage between fights. Under constant pressure the recharge never gets to start.

name: The Adorned
explicitStats: (0-150)% increased Effect of Jewel Socket Passive Skills containing Corrupted Magic Jewels
flavourText:
At their height, the Vaal glittered under the sun.
A decade, a century, an aeon of prosperity...
now nothing more than a passing wonder.
description: (0-150)% increased Effect of Jewel Socket Passive Skills containing Corrupted Magic Jewels

beginner.whatItIs: A diamond jewel that multiplies the effect of jewel socket passives containing corrupted magic jewels, by anything from nothing up to a very large amount.
beginner.whyItMatters: It multiplies other jewels rather than doing anything itself, so its worth is set by how many strong corrupted magic jewels you already own and by its own roll.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a jewel-heavy build with corrupted magic jewels in place, and only with a high roll. At a low roll it is nearly blank.

name: The Anvil
flavourText: Forge your Perseverance on the Anvil of Faith.
description: 10% reduced Movement Speed 10% reduced Skill Speed (25-50)% increased Armour 25% increased Block chance +(5-10)% to maximum Block chance

beginner.whatItIs: A bloodstone amulet that raises maximum life, armour, block chance and your block cap, and slows both your movement and your skills by a tenth.
beginner.whyItMatters: Raising the maximum block chance is rare, because a normal block build hits the cap and then has nowhere left to grow, and this lifts that ceiling.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slow, shield-carrying character that intends to stand still and absorb hits. The speed penalty is painful on anything that needs to reposition.

name: The Auspex
explicitStats: Chance to Deflect is Lucky while on Low Life
Enemies in your Presence gain 1 Gruelling Madness each second
flavourText:
"The boy is a bad omen," he cried. "Ravens gather
before him!" That night, a new raven appeared, and
shadowed the Auspex for the rest of his days.
description: (210-240)% increased Evasion Rating +(70-120) to maximum Life 100% increased Attribute Requirements Chance to Deflect is Lucky while on Low Life Enemies in your Presence gain 1 Gruelling Madness each second

beginner.whatItIs: An exquisite vest with heavy evasion and life that makes your deflection chance lucky while your life is low, and stacks a debuff called Gruelling Madness on enemies near you each second.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lucky deflection rolls twice and keeps the better result, so the chest is at its strongest exactly when you are closest to dying, which is an unusual place to put a defence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five build that deliberately plays at low life. The doubled attribute requirements are steep, so check you can wear it before planning around it.

name: The Barrow Dweller
explicitStats: Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky while you are on Low Life
50% chance to Avoid Death from Hits
flavourText:
In the mists they dwell,
forever hungry,
forever cold.
description: (60-100)% increased Armour and Evasion -(20-10)% to Fire Resistance +50% to Cold Resistance Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky while you are on Low Life 50% chance to Avoid Death from Hits

beginner.whatItIs: An early rogue armour with a large cold resistance bonus that makes enemy damage against you unlucky while you are on low life, and gives a coin-flip chance to survive a hit that would kill you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Both lines only matter at the moment you are about to die, so it is a piece bought entirely for the worst case rather than for a fight you were already winning.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eleven on any character learning content that kills it. The lowered fire resistance is a real cost, so cap fire elsewhere.

name: The Black Cat
explicitStats: Lightning Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky during effect
flavourText:
The most beloved member of every Brinerot crew
is the one that refuses to do any actual work.
description: (10-20)% increased Duration Lightning Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky during effect

beginner.whatItIs: A grounding charm that triggers when you are shocked and makes enemy lightning damage unlucky for its duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: Unlucky damage rolls twice and keeps the lower result, so the charm shrinks the follow-up lightning hits that a shock was about to make much worse.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level thirty-two in lightning-heavy content, where the trigger and the payoff both come from the same source.

name: The Black Doubt
explicitStats: Damage over Time bypasses your Energy Shield
While not on Full Life, Sacrifice 10% of maximum Mana per Second to Recover that much Life
flavourText: Suspicion is a sinister shadow slithering in the soul.
description: (60-100)% increased Energy Shield +(10-30) to Intelligence +(10-20)% to Cold Resistance Damage over Time bypasses your Energy Shield While not on Full Life, Sacrifice 10% of maximum Mana per Second to Recover that much Life

beginner.whatItIs: A hexer's robe with energy shield, intelligence and cold resistance that spends a tenth of your maximum mana each second to heal the same amount of life whenever you are not at full life, and lets damage over time bypass your shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns mana into a life recovery pool, which is powerful on a high-mana caster and dangerous because the shield no longer protects you from anything that ticks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eleven on a caster with a large mana pool and an answer to damage over time. Without either, both halves of this robe work against you.

name: The Black Insignia
explicitStats: Gain Tailwind on Critical Hit, no more than once per second
flavourText:
Brinerot pirates live in a perpetual blaze of glory,
pushing their luck right to the end.
description: (70-100)% increased Evasion Rating (10-20)% increased Rarity of Items found +(15-25)% to Lightning Resistance Gain Tailwind on Critical Hit, no more than once per second Lose all Tailwind when Hit

beginner.whatItIs: A corsair cap with evasion, lightning resistance and item rarity that grants Tailwind on a critical hit, and strips all of it away as soon as you are hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Tailwind speeds up everything you do, so the helmet rewards a critical build that never gets touched and gives nothing to one that trades hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a ranged critical build at level forty-five played at distance. In melee the stacks will be knocked off constantly.

name: The Blood Thorn
flavourText: Touch not the thorn, for only blood and pain await.
description: Adds (8-12) to (16-18) Physical Damage +(10-15) to Strength Causes Bleeding on Hit (4-5) to (8-10) Physical Thorns damage

beginner.whatItIs: A level one wrapped quarterstaff with added physical damage and strength that causes bleeding on every hit and returns physical thorns damage to attackers.
beginner.whyItMatters: Guaranteed bleeding means every swing leaves damage behind, which is a real share of your kill speed in the opening acts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one for levelling a physical melee character, especially against tougher single enemies where the bleed has time to tick.

name: The Brass Dome
explicitStats: Take no Extra Damage from Critical Hits
flavourText: The turtle's shell one day becomes its tomb.
description: (500-600)% increased Armour -(5-1)% to all Maximum Elemental Resistances +(200-300) to Stun Threshold Take no Extra Damage from Critical Hits

beginner.whatItIs: A champion cuirass with an enormous armour bonus and a big stun threshold that removes the extra damage critical hits normally deal, in exchange for lowering all your maximum elemental resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: Critical hits from monsters are what turn a survivable attack into a lethal one, and flattening them makes incoming damage far more predictable than gear alone can.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an armour build at level fifty-eight facing enemies that crit. Only wear it once your elemental resistances can absorb the lowered cap.

name: The Bringer of Rain
explicitStats: You can wield Two-Handed Axes, Maces and Swords in one hand
This item gains bonuses from Socketed Items as though it was a Body Armour
flavourText:
"What lies beneath your feet?!"
"Sacred ground, watered with tears of blood!"
description: (600-800)% increased Armour and Evasion +(200-300) to Accuracy Rating 100% increased Critical Hit Chance (30-60) Life Regeneration per second Can't use Body Armour You can wield Two-Handed Axes, Maces and Swords in one hand This item gains bonuses from Socketed Items as though it was a Body Armour Has 4 Augment Sockets (Hidden)

beginner.whatItIs: A decorated helm with an enormous defence bonus, accuracy, critical chance and heavy regeneration that stops you wearing body armour, lets you hold a two-handed axe, mace or sword in one hand, and takes bonuses from its four sockets as though it were a chest.
beginner.whyItMatters: It replaces your body armour slot with a helmet and changes what you can wield, so it reshapes two parts of your character rather than adding stats to one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level fifty-two melee build willing to give up its chest entirely. Compare its defences against the chest you would otherwise wear before committing.

name: The Burden of Leadership
explicitStats: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Sekhema's Resolve
Rooms are unknown on the Trial Map
This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial
flavourText:
The path forward is unknown,
but someone must lead.
Let it be the best of us.
description: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Sekhema's Resolve Rooms are unknown on the Trial Map This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial

beginner.whatItIs: A tapestry relic applied to a Trial of the Sekhemas that makes its final boss drop a specific unique, and hides the room layout for the whole run.
beginner.whyItMatters: It buys a guaranteed reward with information, so you know what you will win but not what you are walking into.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When you want that particular unique and are confident enough to run a trial blind. The relic is destroyed on use, so bring it only for a run you expect to finish.

name: The Burden of Shadows
explicitStats: Skill Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs
Skills gain 1% of Damage as Chaos Damage per 3 Life Cost
flavourText:
Nothingness is loathe to relinquish its grip.
Every moment is a struggle to exist.
description: (20-30)% increased Cast Speed Skill Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs Skills gain 1% of Damage as Chaos Damage per 3 Life Cost

beginner.whatItIs: A chiming staff with high cast speed that converts all of your skill mana costs into life costs, and adds chaos damage in proportion to how much life each skill costs.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes your life pool the resource you cast with and the reason your spells hit harder, so an expensive skill is both riskier and stronger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level seventy-two caster with a big life pool and strong recovery. Without recovery, casting will kill you faster than any monster.

name: The Burrower
explicitStats: Lightning Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky
flavourText:
It coils deeper and deeper
It slithers between thoughts
It lies beneath the valley
It lies in our minds
description: -10% to Cold Resistance +(20-30)% to Lightning Resistance (30-50)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Lightning Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky

beginner.whatItIs: A topaz ring with heavy lightning resistance and mana regeneration that makes enemy lightning damage unlucky, at the cost of a little cold resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: Unlucky damage rolls twice and keeps the lower result, so it shaves the top off lightning hits in a way resistance alone cannot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen in lightning-heavy content. It is worth most against enemies whose lightning damage varies wildly between hits.

name: The Changing Seasons
explicitStats: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Sandstorm Visage
This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial
flavourText:
All rejoiced when Solerai and Lundara shattered the grey sky,
but with the cold banished, sandier climes began to creep in...
description: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Sandstorm Visage Cannot restore Honour This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial

beginner.whatItIs: A seal relic that makes the Trial's final boss drop a specific helmet, and stops you restoring honour during the run.
beginner.whyItMatters: Honour is the resource that ends a trial when it runs out, so being unable to restore it turns every avoidable hit into permanent progress lost.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a clean, practised trial run when you want that helmet. It is destroyed on use, so do not spend it while still learning the layout.

name: The Coming Calamity
explicitStats: Enemies in your Presence have no Elemental Resistances
flavourText:
Whiff of cold, tiny spark, faintest flicker in the dark.
Embers swirl, ice takes form, sky exposed - Death's perfect storm.
Frost and thunder, flames shine bright, ruin walks the land tonight.
By your hand they dance and bend, wield them and brook no end.
description: +(30-40)% to all Elemental Resistances Herald Skills deal (50-100)% increased Damage Enemies in your Presence have no Elemental Resistances

beginner.whatItIs: A heroic armour with life and a large elemental resistance bonus that greatly increases herald skill damage and strips the elemental resistances off every enemy near you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing enemy resistance rather than reducing it is a very large damage multiplier for anyone in the fight dealing elemental damage, including your allies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five elemental build running heralds. On a physical or chaos build only the defences on it are doing any work.

name: The Covenant
explicitStats: 10% of Spell Damage Leeched as Life
Skills Gain 100% of Mana Cost as Extra Life Cost
flavourText:
My Soul is your Strength
My Price is your Blood
description: (100-150)% increased Energy Shield +(100-150) to maximum Life 10% of Spell Damage Leeched as Life Skills Gain 100% of Mana Cost as Extra Life Cost

beginner.whatItIs: An altar robe with energy shield and life that leeches life from your spell damage, and makes every skill pay its mana cost again in life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns casting into a self-damaging act that pays for itself only while you are hitting things, so your safety is tied directly to landing spells rather than to your defences.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spell build at level forty that hits reliably and has a large life pool. Against a boss you cannot reach it will drain you with nothing coming back.

name: The Dancing Dervish
explicitStats: Triggers Level 15 Manifest Dancing Dervishes on Rampage
Manifested Dancing Dervishes die when Rampage ends
Melee Hits count as Rampage Kills
flavourText:
Take your partner by the hand,
Keep your steps in time.
Swing together, spin apart,
And dance with death sublime.
description: Triggers Level 15 Manifest Dancing Dervishes on Rampage Cannot be used while Manifested Manifested Dancing Dervishes die when Rampage ends Melee Hits count as Rampage Kills Rampage

beginner.whatItIs: A scimitar that summons dancing swords to fight for you when you enter Rampage, and cannot be wielded while they are manifested.
beginner.whyItMatters: Your weapon leaves your hands to become minions, so you swap from attacking yourself to commanding what used to be your sword until the rampage ends.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen in dense content where you can keep a rampage running. In a boss fight with nothing to kill, the swords never appear.

name: The Dancing Mirage
explicitStats: 20% less Damage taken if you have not been Hit Recently
100% increased Evasion Rating if you have been Hit Recently
flavourText: Be not where death falls.
description: (150-200)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield +(10-20)% to Lightning Resistance 20% less Damage taken if you have not been Hit Recently 100% increased Evasion Rating if you have been Hit Recently

beginner.whatItIs: A wayfarer jacket with evasion and energy shield that reduces all damage taken while you have gone untouched, and doubles your evasion rating for a while after you are hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: The two lines cover each other: you are hard to damage while clean and hard to hit again once you have been caught, so there is no window where the jacket does nothing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-eight on any evasion character. It is one of the more forgiving defensive chests for a player still learning an encounter.

name: The Dark Defiler
explicitStats: Gain 5% of Damage as Chaos Damage per Undead Minion
flavourText: Rare is the Necromancer who leads his undead armies from the front.
description: +(20-30) to maximum Mana +(5-10) to Intelligence (10-30)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Gain 5% of Damage as Chaos Damage per Undead Minion

beginner.whatItIs: A level one rattling sceptre with mana, intelligence and mana regeneration that adds chaos damage to your hits for every undead minion you have.
beginner.whyItMatters: It scales with your army size rather than with any stat on the weapon, so a summoner's damage grows as its minion count does.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level one on a build raising undead minions. With no minions the sceptre adds nothing at all.

name: The Desperate Alliance
explicitStats: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Against the Darkness
Zarokh, the Temporal deals 100% more Damage
Zarokh, the Temporal takes 75% less Damage
This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial
flavourText:
By fire and ice, perhaps the end of the world.
They did not fall on their knees and lament.
description: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Against the Darkness Zarokh, the Temporal deals 100% more Damage Zarokh, the Temporal takes 75% less Damage This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial

beginner.whatItIs: A vase relic that makes the Trial's final boss drop a specific jewel while dealing far more damage and taking far less of it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the hardest of the relic trades: the reward is fixed but the fight becomes a genuine test of both your damage and your survival.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a character that already beats the boss comfortably. It is destroyed on use, so a failed attempt costs the relic as well as the run.

name: The Devouring Diadem
explicitStats: Every 3 seconds, Consume a nearby Corpse to Recover 20% of maximum Life
flavourText: The spirit hungers for the flesh.
description: (60-100)% increased Energy Shield +(40-60) to maximum Life +(10-20) to Intelligence +(13-19)% to Chaos Resistance Every 3 seconds, Consume a nearby Corpse to Recover 20% of maximum Life

beginner.whatItIs: A wicker tiara with energy shield, life, intelligence and chaos resistance that eats a nearby corpse every three seconds to heal a fifth of your maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: A fifth of your life every three seconds is very strong recovery for a level ten item, but it depends entirely on there being bodies on the ground.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level ten while clearing packs. In a boss fight with no corpses around the healing simply does not happen.

name: The Empty Roar
implicitStats: Strikes deal Splash damage to targets within 1.8 metres
explicitStats: Leeches 10% of Physical Damage as Life
(10-20)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit
All Attacks count as Empowered Attacks
flavourText: Secrecy and silence are powers all their own.
description: Adds (25-35) to (40-50) Physical Damage Leeches 10% of Physical Damage as Life (10-20)% chance to cause Bleeding on Hit All Attacks count as Empowered Attacks Cannot use Warcries

beginner.whatItIs: A cultist greathammer with splash damage, added physical damage and life leech whose attacks all count as empowered, and which stops you using warcries.
beginner.whyItMatters: Permanently empowered attacks are a large constant damage gain, paid for by giving up warcries entirely rather than by a stat penalty.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level twenty-two on a melee build that does not rely on warcries. On a warcry build it removes your main mechanic.

name: The Eternal Spark
explicitStats: 40% increased Mana Regeneration Rate while stationary
flavourText:
A flash of blue, a stormcloud's kiss,
her motionless dance the pulse of bliss
description: (50-70)% increased Energy Shield +5% to Maximum Lightning Resistance +(20-30)% to Lightning Resistance 40% increased Mana Regeneration Rate 40% increased Mana Regeneration Rate while stationary

beginner.whatItIs: A crystal focus with energy shield and a large amount of lightning resistance that also raises your maximum lightning resistance and doubles up on mana regeneration while standing still.
beginner.whyItMatters: Raising the maximum resistance is worth far more than the flat resistance next to it, because it lifts a ceiling most characters have already reached.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster from level twenty-six going into lightning-heavy content, especially one that fights from a fixed spot.

name: The Everlasting Gaze
explicitStats: Gain (4-6)% of maximum Mana as Extra maximum Energy Shield
flavourText:
What they saw was what they believed, and
they believed Lunaris had not abandoned them.
description: +(40-60) to maximum Mana (40-60)% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Gain (4-6)% of maximum Mana as Extra maximum Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: An azure amulet available from level one that adds maximum mana, a large boost to mana regeneration, and turns a slice of your mana pool into extra energy shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes mana do two jobs, so every mana roll you pick up elsewhere quietly becomes defence as well as fuel for your skills.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a caster the moment you find one and keep it through the early acts, since a starting character has very little energy shield from any other source.

name: The Fall of the Axe
implicitStats: Used when you are affected by a Slow
flavourText:
"When the headsman's blade swings,
your last moments stretch to eternity."
- Vorm, the Twice-Pardoned
description: Grants Onslaught during effect

beginner.whatItIs: A silver charm that triggers whenever a slow is applied to you and grants Onslaught for its duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: Onslaught raises attack, cast and movement speed at once, so the charm answers a slow by making you faster than you were before it landed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level ten in any content that slows you, which makes it one of the most reliably triggered charms for a melee character.

name: The Flesh Poppet
explicitStats: Copy a random Modifier from each enemy in your Presence when you Shapeshift to an Animal form
Modifiers gained this way are lost after 30 seconds or when you next Shapeshift
flavourText:
Long ago, the witches of the Azak Tribe learned
how to tap into the flow of Vivid lifeforce to
'cooperate' with their enemies... forcefully.
description: (90-120)% increased Physical Damage (7-13)% increased Attack Speed +(7-13) to all Attributes (40-30)% reduced Presence Area of Effect Copy a random Modifier from each enemy in your Presence when you Shapeshift to an Animal form Modifiers gained this way are lost after 30 seconds or when you next Shapeshift

beginner.whatItIs: A vicious talisman with physical damage, attack speed and attributes that copies a random modifier from each enemy near you when you shapeshift, keeping them for half a minute.
beginner.whyItMatters: Your buffs are decided by what you are fighting, so the talisman is unpredictable by design and rewards shifting in the middle of a dangerous pack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty shapeshifting build fighting rare monsters with modifiers worth stealing.

name: The Gnashing Sash
explicitStats: Lose 5% of maximum Life per second
Life Recovery from Flasks can Overflow Maximum Life
flavourText:
"Ghorr knows only hunger, only ravenous feasting.
It will consume all that lives, and more!"
- Rantings of a Templar prisoner, page fourteen
description: (15-35)% increased Flask Life Recovery rate +(17-23)% to Chaos Resistance Lose 5% of maximum Life per second Life Recovery from Flasks can Overflow Maximum Life

beginner.whatItIs: A wide belt with chaos resistance and faster flask healing that costs you five percent of your maximum life per second and lets flask recovery push your life above its normal maximum.
beginner.whyItMatters: Overflowing the life cap gives you a buffer no other item hands out, but you are paying a constant bleed for it, so the belt only works while the flask is flowing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character with strong flask uptime from level sixty. Without charges to keep drinking the drain will simply kill you.

name: The Grand Project
explicitStats: Can only be applied to Precursor Tower Maps
Completing the Tower makes all nearby Maps accessible
flavourText: "I see a pattern in these towers. Whoever the Precursors were, they sought to master this world, to shape it as they saw fit. My people had the same ambitions..."
description: Can only be applied to Precursor Tower Maps Completing the Tower makes all nearby Maps accessible

beginner.whatItIs: An irradiated tablet with one use that only applies to precursor tower maps, and makes completing that tower open every nearby map.
beginner.whyItMatters: Opening a whole region at once saves a long sequence of individual maps, which is a large time saving rather than a power one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a tower positioned to unlock a dense cluster of maps. On an isolated tower the single use is wasted.

name: The Hammer of Faith
explicitStats: Every 10 seconds, gain a random non-damaging Shrine buff for 20 seconds
flavourText:
The secret Order endured by publicly
praying however the Templars demanded.
One day, justice would fall upon them...
description: (300-350)% increased Physical Damage 10% reduced Attack Speed +10% to all Elemental Resistances 50% increased Mana Regeneration Rate Every 10 seconds, gain a random non-damaging Shrine buff for 20 seconds

beginner.whatItIs: A giant maul with very high physical damage, elemental resistance and mana regeneration that grants a random non-damaging shrine buff every ten seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shrine buff is normally something you find in the world, and having one running almost constantly is a steady advantage with no setup at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five two-handed build, and it is at its best in long fights where the buff keeps refreshing.

name: The Hollow Mask
explicitStats: Remnants you create affect Allies in your Presence as well as you when collected
(80-100)% increased Reservation Efficiency of Remnant Skills
flavourText: The roots burrow deeper, unveiling the wood's bounty...
description: +(60-80) to maximum Life 15% additional Physical Damage Reduction -10% to all Elemental Resistances +13% to Chaos Resistance Remnants you create affect Allies in your Presence as well as you when collected (80-100)% increased Reservation Efficiency of Remnant Skills

beginner.whatItIs: A hewn mask with life, chaos resistance and flat physical damage reduction that shares the remnants you create with allies in your presence and makes remnant skills far cheaper to reserve.
beginner.whyItMatters: Sharing remnants turns a personal pickup into a party buff, so the mask is worth more with people around you than it is alone.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For group play from level five on a remnant build. The elemental resistance penalty has to be covered elsewhere.

name: The Infinite Pursuit
explicitStats: (80-100)% increased Chance to be afflicted by Ailments when Hit
25% increased Movement Speed while affected by an Ailment
flavourText: We move to be closer to her, but the distance yet grows.
description: 10% increased Movement Speed (100-150)% increased Armour +(80-100) to maximum Life (80-100)% increased Chance to be afflicted by Ailments when Hit 25% increased Movement Speed while affected by an Ailment

beginner.whatItIs: Bronze greaves with armour, life and movement speed that make you much more likely to be afflicted by ailments, and much faster while any ailment is on you.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes a downside into your speed source, so the boots are fastest exactly in the fights where you are being frozen, shocked or ignited.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a character that can shrug off ailments, through content that applies them constantly. On a fragile build the added affliction chance is dangerous.

name: The Knight-errant
flavourText: Some search forever for their path.
description: 10% increased Movement Speed (30-50)% increased Armour and Evasion +(30-50) to Stun Threshold +(30-50) to Ailment Threshold Iron Reflexes

beginner.whatItIs: Early mail sabatons with movement speed, armour, evasion and both stun and ailment thresholds that grant Iron Reflexes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Iron Reflexes converts all of your evasion rating into armour, which is a whole change of defensive style available from level six rather than deep in the passive tree.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character that wants armour but has picked up evasion gear or passives early. It is a straight loss on a build that wants to keep dodging.

name: The Last Flame
explicitStats: Cannot be used with Trials below level 80
This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial
flavourText: In the coldest depths of the Winter of the World, overrun by darkness and fighting to the last, life itself clung to existence by the barest remaining thread.
description: Zarokh, the Temporal drops Temporalis Damage taken cannot be Absorbed Maximum Honour is 1 Cannot be used with Trials below level 80 This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial

beginner.whatItIs: An incense relic that makes the Trial's final boss drop a specific body armour, sets your maximum honour to one, stops damage being absorbed, and only works on trials above level eighty.
beginner.whyItMatters: With a single point of honour, one avoidable hit anywhere in the run ends it, so the relic asks for a flawless trial rather than a survivable one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only for a run you expect to take no avoidable damage in at all. It is the least forgiving of the relics and it is destroyed either way.

name: The Last Lament
explicitStats: Leeches (5-10)% of Physical Damage as Life
(10-20)% chance to load a bolt into all Crossbow skills on Kill
Sacrifice 300 Life to not consume the last bolt when firing
flavourText:
"And here we shall remain...
trapped in our symphony of eternal anguish.
Artist and Composer, their fates entwined for all of time."
- Adamantia Brektov, the Composer
description: (250-300)% increased Physical Damage (10-20)% increased Attack Speed (60-40)% reduced Reload Speed Leeches (5-10)% of Physical Damage as Life (10-20)% chance to load a bolt into all Crossbow skills on Kill Sacrifice 300 Life to not consume the last bolt when firing

beginner.whatItIs: A desolate crossbow with very high physical damage and life leech that reloads far more slowly, sometimes loads a bolt into every crossbow skill on kill, and lets you spend three hundred life to keep your last bolt.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets you keep firing past the point where you should have reloaded, paying in life instead of time, which suits a leeching build that gets that life straight back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level seventy-seven crossbow build with strong leech and a large life pool. Without leech the life cost stacks up quickly.

name: The Lethal Draw
implicitStats: Gain (2-3) Life per Enemy Hit with Attacks
explicitStats: Gain 5 Life per Enemy Hit with Attacks
Bow Attacks consume 10% of your maximum Life Flask Charges if possible to deal added Physical damage equal to (5-10)% of Flask's Life Recovery amount
flavourText: Life and death ooze from the same sap.
description: (5-10)% increased Attack Speed Gain 5 Life per Enemy Hit with Attacks (15-25)% chance to Pierce an Enemy Bow Attacks consume 10% of your maximum Life Flask Charges if possible to deal added Physical damage equal to (5-10)% of Flask's Life Recovery amount

beginner.whatItIs: A sacral quiver with attack speed, life on hit and a chance to pierce whose bow attacks spend life flask charges to add physical damage based on what the flask would have healed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts your healing into damage, so the better your life flask is, the harder you hit and the less recovery you have left in reserve.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a bow build with strong flask charge generation. It is dangerous in fights where you need those charges to survive.

name: The Master's Reach
explicitStats: Reveal Weaknesses against Rare and Unique enemies
Eat a Soul on Hitting an enemy with an Open Weakness
(80-100)% of damagen taken from enemies with an Open Weakness Recouped as Life
flavourText:
The Master's tether wraps itself around the soul.
Should he be denied, he will unmercifully set it free.
description: (200-300)% increased Armour and Energy Shield +(75-125) to maximum Life +(15-25) to Intelligence Reveal Weaknesses against Rare and Unique enemies Eat a Soul on Hitting an enemy with an Open Weakness (80-100)% of damagen taken from enemies with an Open Weakness Recouped as Life

beginner.whatItIs: Tethering bands with heavy defences and life that reveal weaknesses on rare and unique enemies, let you eat a soul when you hit through one, and recoup almost all damage those enemies deal to you as life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes fighting a rare or boss monster safer rather than faster, because most of what it hits you for comes back over time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level sixty-five character taking on rare and unique enemies. Against ordinary monsters none of the three lines apply.

name: The Mutable Star
explicitStats: (50-30)% reduced Duration of Bleeding on You
Defend against Hits as though you had 1% more Armour per 1% current Energy Shield
flavourText:
Through every great purge, and every fiery inquisition,
the Twilight Order endured in secret.
description: (100-150)% increased Armour and Energy Shield (50-100)% increased Energy Shield Recharge Rate (25-35) Life Regeneration per second (50-30)% reduced Duration of Bleeding on You (30-50)% reduced Ignite Duration on you Defend against Hits as though you had 1% more Armour per 1% current Energy Shield

beginner.whatItIs: A cleric vestment with armour, energy shield and heavy life regeneration that treats every point of your current energy shield as extra armour, and shortens bleeds and ignites on you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Armour and energy shield normally sit in separate defensive worlds, and this makes a full shield actively improve how well armour absorbs a hit rather than just adding a buffer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an armour and energy shield hybrid at level forty-five. Its value drops sharply once your shield spends most of a fight empty.

name: The Ordained
implicitStats: 25% increased Melee Strike Range with this weapon
explicitStats: Life Leech recovers based on your Lightning damage as well as Physical damage
Create a Fragment of Divinity in your Presence every 4 seconds
flavourText: May the Lightless drown in the violence of His devotion.
description: (150-250)% increased Physical Damage Adds 1 to (200-300) Lightning Damage +(5-8)% to Critical Hit Chance Life Leech recovers based on your Lightning damage as well as Physical damage Create a Fragment of Divinity in your Presence every 4 seconds

beginner.whatItIs: A grand spear with very high physical damage, a large added lightning roll and extra reach that lets your leech recover from lightning damage as well as physical, and drops a Fragment of Divinity near you every few seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Leech normally only counts physical damage, so a hybrid physical and lightning spear can sustain itself off both halves of its output instead of one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level seventy-nine spear build mixing physical and lightning damage. A pure lightning build gains from the leech line but loses the physical scaling.

name: The Pandemonius
flavourText:
A single moment sets in motion an eternal fall,
beneath which all are buried.
description: +(50-100)% to Cold Resistance Damage Penetrates 75% Cold Resistance Blind Chilled enemies on Hit

beginner.whatItIs: A lapis amulet that hands you a huge amount of cold resistance, makes your damage ignore three quarters of the enemy's cold resistance, and blinds anything you hit that is chilled.
beginner.whyItMatters: Penetration works on targets that resist cold heavily, which is exactly where a cold build normally stalls, and the blind turns your damage skill into a defensive one against melee monsters.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build from level fifty-two, especially in content full of cold-resistant monsters. Make sure something in your setup actually chills, or the blind never triggers.

name: The Peacemaker's Draught
explicitStats: Zarokh, the Temporal drops an additional Barya
This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial
flavourText:
Centuries of peace brought immense wealth to Keth,
but many worried that it had also left the people soft.
description: Zarokh, the Temporal drops an additional Barya Your Defences are zero This item is destroyed when applied to a Trial

beginner.whatItIs: An amphora relic that makes the Trial's final boss drop an extra Barya while reducing your defences to zero.
beginner.whyItMatters: Zero defences means every hit lands in full, so the extra reward is bought with a fight where nothing protects you but movement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a run you can complete without being hit. It is destroyed on use, so save it for a trial you know well.

name: The Prisoner's Manacles
explicitStats: Debuffs you inflict have (20-30)% increased Slow Magnitude
flavourText:
Only once did Maligaro wonder if he'd gone too far.
His greatest success took three entire legions to capture.
description: (200-300)% increased Armour and Energy Shield +100 to maximum Life 100% increased Attribute Requirements +(20-40)% to Lightning Resistance (15-30) Life Regeneration per second Debuffs you inflict have (20-30)% increased Slow Magnitude Cannot Immobilise enemies

beginner.whatItIs: Kalguuran cuffs with very high defences, life regeneration and lightning resistance that deepen the slows in your debuffs but stop you immobilising enemies, with doubled attribute requirements.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slowing harder while never immobilising keeps enemies moving but sluggish, which suits a build that wants time to land hits rather than one that wants targets pinned.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty-five debuff build that does not rely on immobilisation. Check you can meet the doubled requirements before planning for them.

name: The Rat Cage
explicitStats: 100% of Fire Damage from Hits taken as Physical Damage
flavourText:
The truth lies inside every man, if you dig around.
Many a confession was found in the bowels of Axiom.
description: (100-150)% increased Evasion Rating +300 to maximum Life 25% reduced Attribute Requirements 100% of Fire Damage from Hits taken as Physical Damage

beginner.whatItIs: A scout's vest with evasion and a flat three hundred maximum life that lowers attribute requirements and converts every point of fire damage you take from hits into physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Fire is the element most likely to arrive as one huge hit, and turning it physical hands it to your armour instead of your fire resistance, which is a different and often better wall.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an armoured character at level thirty-three going into fire-heavy content. Without armour to absorb it, the conversion just makes fire damage harder to reduce.

name: The Raven's Flock
explicitStats: Minions have (10-20)% chance to inflict Gruelling Madness on Hit
(30-50)% increased Spirit Reservation Efficiency of Skills
flavourText:
"Where the boy went, ravens gathered,
feasting on misery. His vile influence
spread, swift as the carnage they wrought."
description: (8-16)% increased Cast Speed +(20-30) to Intelligence Minions deal (80-120)% increased Damage Minions have (10-20)% chance to inflict Gruelling Madness on Hit (30-50)% increased Spirit Reservation Efficiency of Skills

beginner.whatItIs: A perching staff with cast speed and intelligence that greatly increases minion damage, gives minions a chance to inflict Gruelling Madness, and improves how efficiently your skills reserve spirit.
beginner.whyItMatters: The reservation efficiency is what lets a summoner field another aura or another minion type, on top of the raw damage bonus.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build at level sixty-five. It does nothing at all for a caster fighting alone.

name: The Searing Touch
flavourText:
Burn to cinders, scar and maim,
Rule a world, bathed in flame.
description: (80-120)% increased Fire Damage (10-20)% increased Cast Speed 100% increased Flammability Magnitude 100% increased Ignite Magnitude

beginner.whatItIs: A pyrophyte staff with a large fire damage and cast speed bonus that doubles both flammability magnitude and ignite magnitude.
beginner.whyItMatters: Deeper flammability strips more fire resistance while deeper ignites burn harder, so the staff multiplies both halves of a fire build's damage at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level sixteen on a fire caster that ignites and curses. On any other element the staff does nothing.

name: The Sentry
flavourText:
The night Draven attacked,
Erian was asleep at his post.
description: No Physical Damage Adds (25-32) to (40-50) Fire Damage +(30-50) to Accuracy Rating +20% to Fire Resistance 100% increased Flammability Magnitude 30% increased Light Radius

beginner.whatItIs: A gothic quarterstaff with no physical damage at all, large added fire damage, accuracy, fire resistance and doubled flammability magnitude.
beginner.whyItMatters: Deeper flammability strips more fire resistance off the target, which multiplies the fire damage of everything you and your party do to it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level eleven on a fire build that applies flammability. Physical scaling on your tree does nothing for this weapon.

name: The Smiling Knight
explicitStats: Aggravate Bleeding on targets you Critically Hit with Attacks
flavourText:
He never spoke a word. His opponents imagined
their own personal mockeries, most cruel.
description: (150-200)% increased Armour and Evasion +(50-100) to Accuracy Rating (15-25)% increased Critical Hit Chance Aggravate Bleeding on targets you Critically Hit with Attacks

beginner.whatItIs: A cowled helm with armour, evasion, accuracy and critical hit chance that aggravates bleeding on anything you critically hit with an attack.
beginner.whyItMatters: Aggravated bleeding keeps ticking at its full rate even while the target is standing still, which is otherwise the main way monsters escape bleed damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical bleed build at level twenty-six. Without both a bleed source and reliable crits the helmet's line never fires.

name: The Sunken Vessel
explicitStats: Physical Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky
Convert All Armour to Evasion Rating
flavourText:
"What are you lot looking at? We're
under fire! Get to your stations!"
- Captain Sventura, the Unlucky
description: (120-180)% increased Armour and Evasion +(80-120) to maximum Life 30% reduced Life Recovery rate 33% chance to avoid Projectiles Physical Damage of Enemies Hitting you is Unlucky Convert All Armour to Evasion Rating

beginner.whatItIs: A knight armour that converts all of its armour into evasion rating, makes enemy physical hits unlucky, gives a third chance to avoid projectiles, and slows your life recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: Unlucky physical damage rolls twice and takes the lower result, so the chest quietly shaves the top off every physical hit rather than adding a flat buffer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an evasion character at level forty-five facing physical and projectile damage. The reduced life recovery makes it a poor fit for a flask-dependent build.

name: The Surrender
explicitStats: Recover 4% of maximum Life when you Block
flavourText:
Our hearts cry out
but are silenced by our flesh
and so we give up our flesh.
description: (40-60)% increased Block chance (150-200)% increased Armour +(150-200) to Stun Threshold Recover 4% of maximum Life when you Block

beginner.whatItIs: A vaal tower shield with a very large block chance and armour bonus, high stun threshold, and a heal for a share of your maximum life on every block.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns blocking into recovery, so a character that blocks often is healing continuously rather than only avoiding damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level seventy-five block build facing many attacks. Against a single slow boss the heal fires too rarely to matter.

name: The Taming
explicitStats: (10-20)% increased Damage for each type of Elemental Ailment on Enemy
Wind Skills which can be boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces count as being boosted by Ignited, Shocked, and Chilled Ground
Wind Skills which can be boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces can be boosted by multiple Elemental Ground Surfaces
flavourText:
"Moon after moon did Berek make fools
Of the great and Untamed Three
Until malice for a Brother
Slew the hatred of the Other
And Berek did hunt
Alone and free."
- Berek and the Untamed
description: +(10-20)% to all Elemental Resistances (10-20)% increased Damage for each type of Elemental Ailment on Enemy Wind Skills which can be boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces count as being boosted by Ignited, Shocked, and Chilled Ground Wind Skills which can be boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces can be boosted by multiple Elemental Ground Surfaces

beginner.whatItIs: A prismatic ring with a large elemental resistance bonus that raises your damage for every different elemental ailment on the enemy, and lets wind skills be boosted by several elemental ground surfaces at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: Applying three different ailments to one target is worth far more than stacking one, so the ring rewards a build that spreads ignite, shock and chill together.
beginner.whenToUseIt: From level forty-two on a build that can inflict at least two ailments. With one ailment the damage bonus barely moves.

name: The Three Dragons
explicitStats: Fire Damage from Hits Contributes to Shock Chance instead of Flammability and Ignite Magnitudes
Cold Damage from Hits Contributes to Flammability and Ignite Magnitudes instead of Chill Magnitude or Freeze Buildup
Lightning Damage from Hits Contributes to Freeze Buildup instead of Shock Chance
flavourText:
"The ice seared his naked feet
As the lightning stilled his heart,
But it was the flames upon his lover's face
That roused him to vengeance."
- From 'The Three Dragons' by Victario of Sarn
description: (40-60)% increased Evasion and Energy Shield +(10-20)% to all Elemental Resistances Fire Damage from Hits Contributes to Shock Chance instead of Flammability and Ignite Magnitudes Cold Damage from Hits Contributes to Flammability and Ignite Magnitudes instead of Chill Magnitude or Freeze Buildup Lightning Damage from Hits Contributes to Freeze Buildup instead of Shock Chance

beginner.whatItIs: A solid mask with defences and elemental resistance that rotates which ailment each element builds: fire shocks, cold ignites, and lightning freezes.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a build apply an ailment it has no access to, so a fire character can shock and a lightning character can freeze, without changing its damage type.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a level forty-five elemental build whose damage is one element but whose payoff wants a different ailment.

name: The Unborn Lich
